Connect applications to Ethos Integration

Configure applications to integrate with other applications through Ethos Integration.

Connect Banner to Ethos Integration

Set up Banner APIs and messaging components to support messaging between Banner and other applications using Ellucian Ethos Integration.

Banner setup checklist

The checklist below lists the steps needed to set up Banner in Ethos Integration, and identifies which steps are required to support each of the mechanisms by which other applications get data from Banner through Ethos Integration: by making proxy API requests to Banner, making GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access, or subscribing to changes published by Banner.

You only need to perform the setup required for your integration. For example, if your integration requires only API requests, you can skip some of the setup that supports GraphQL requests and publish/subscribe, such as installing and configuring the Ellucian Messaging Service, Ellucian Message Adapter, and Banner Event Publisher.

Messaging component considerations

This section provides considerations for deploying the software components that connect Banner to Ellucian Ethos Integration.

Connecting Banner to Ellucian Ethos Integration requires the following software components.

  • The application's Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs (the Banner Student API).
  • The Ellucian Message Adapter.
  • The application's event generator, Banner Event Publisher (BEP).
  • The Ellucian Messaging Service.

Some of these components may already be installed at your institution to support other integrations. Currently the messaging components are only used by the Banner Ethos APIs. The Business Process APIs do not currently use these components.

The messaging components may be installed on a single server to reduce the number of servers in your environment. Alternately, you can co-locate the event generator and Ellucian Messaging Service on one server and the Ellucian Message Adapter and application APIs on another server.

Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs

APIs that support the Ellucian Ethos Data Model are available for Banner. API packages must be downloaded and installed separately from your Banner installation.

Applications that integrate with Banner using Ellucian Ethos Integration may require a more recent version of the APIs than the minimum version. Review the documentation of the application that you plan to integrate to understand its dependencies on specific Ellucian Ethos Data Model entities.

Event Generator

Data changes in Banner are captured and communicated by the BEP business event generator.

The event generator may already be installed at your institution to support other integrations. The installed software can be used to support Ellucian Ethos Integration. Configuration may be required so that business events are published to the appropriate queues for each support integration.

The event generator for Banner, BEP, is delivered as part of the Banner deployment.

Ellucian Messaging Service

The Ellucian Messaging Service is message queuing software that provides a decoupled channel of communication between the event generator and the Ellucian Message Adapter.

The Ellucian Messaging Service may already be installed at your institution to support other integrations. The installed software can be used to support integration with Ellucian Ethos Integration. Configuration will required to create a queue for the event generator to publish business events for the Ellucian Message Adapter.

Ellucian Message Adapter

The Ellucian Message Adapter is the software component that publishes change notifications to Ellucian Ethos Integration for Banner. Previous versions of the Ellucian Message Adapter were used to support integration between Banner and Ellucian Elevate.

The Ellucian Message Adapter can be configured to publish messages to Ellucian Ethos Integration or to the Ellucian Messaging Service for legacy integration with Elevate, but not both. If you need to publish messages to both destinations, two instances of the Ellucian Message Adapter are required.

Banner Business Process APIs

The Banner Business Process APIs expose HTTP / JSON functionality on top of existing Banner Administrative Pages. For the current release, there are no additional messaging components required.

Banner and Colleague messaging components

This section provides an overview of the software components that collaborate to connect Banner or Colleague to Ellucian Ethos Integration.

Connecting Banner or Colleague to Ellucian Ethos Integration requires additional software components. The following components work together to adapt the applications to the messaging model and data format used by Ellucian Ethos Integration.

  • The application's Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs.
  • The application's event generator:
    • Banner Event Publisher (BEP) for Banner.
    • Envision Data Exchange (EDX) for Colleague.
  • The Ellucian Messaging Service.
  • The Ellucian Message Adapter.

All of these software components are available on the Ellucian Download Center or SA Valet for Colleague clients, and require no additional licensing.

The following diagram shows the individual software components and their use in the publish/subscribe and request/reply messaging.

Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs

The Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs simplify and standardize integration with external applications by exposing Banner or Colleague data in the common Ellucian Ethos Data Model format.

The APIs enable request/reply messaging from external systems through the Proxy service of Ellucian Ethos Integration. The request/reply messaging flow is shown by the blue arrows and numbers in the diagram above. The APIs are also used by the Ellucian Message Adapter when it publishes change notifications to the Publisher service of Ellucian Ethos Integration. The publish and subscribe messaging flow is shown by the green arrows and numbers in the diagram.

The Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs for Colleague are included in the Colleague Web API beginning with release 1.11. The Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs for Banner are included in separate API packages for each functional area beginning with Banner Student 9.5.

Note: New APIs continue to be added and you should upgrade your API installations to take advantage of the latest integration capabilities.

Event Generator (BEP or EDX)

The event generators monitor database changes and trigger publication of messages to external systems. The event generator for Banner is the Banner Event Publisher (BEP). The event generator for Colleague is Envision Data Exchange (EDX).

The event generators publish data changes as rapidly as possible. They publish data as generic business events that contain only a limited amount of data to make them efficient and allow them to be used for a variety of integrations. A separate software component is required to turn these generic business events into a message that has relevance to an external application. Message queuing software is used to avoid tight coupling between the event generator and the software that processes the business events.

Ellucian Messaging Service

The Ellucian Messaging Service is message queuing software that decouples the event generator for Banner or Colleague from the software that processes the business events. Business events created by BEP or EDX are published to a defined queue in the Ellucian Messaging Service and are read by the software that processes business events asynchronously, but in the order in which they occurred. This allows the event generator and the software that processes business events to work at their own pace while maintaining the original order in which data changes occurred.

Ellucian Message Adapter

The Ellucian Message Adapter is the common software component that publishes data changes from Banner or Colleague to Ellucian Ethos Integration. Publishing change notifications is a requirement for these applications when they are configured as authoritative for Ellucian Ethos Data Model entities.

The Ellucian Message Adapter requires several other components to operate. The Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs must be installed and available to the Ellucian Message Adapter for it to retrieve the appropriate Ellucian Ethos Data Model format to publish. The Ellucian Message Adapter is also dependent on the Ellucian Messaging Service and the event generator for Banner or Colleague. These components notify the Ellucian Message Adapter to publish a change notification whenever data in Banner or Colleague changes.

Understanding the Message Flow

The diagram above shows both the request/reply and the publish and subscribe messaging flow through Ellucian Ethos Integration.

The blue arrows show a service invocation being made to the Proxy service by an external application that is not authoritative for an Ellucian Ethos Data Model entity (1). Based on the configuration, the Proxy service forwards the request to the exposed API of the application that is authoritative for the entity in the request (2). The response that is returned to the Proxy service (3) is sent to the application that originated the service invocation (4).

The green arrows show the publish and subscribe flow which involves all of the messaging components. BEP or EDX is responsible for monitoring Banner or Colleague for data changes. The event generator posts a data change to the Ellucian Messaging Service (EMS) in a defined business event format (1). The Ellucian Message Adapter (EMA) is a consumer of the business event message published by BEP or EDX (2). When the EMA consumes a business event, it invokes the appropriate Banner or Colleague API (3) to get the full representation of the associated Ellucian Ethos Data Model entity (4). The EMA then posts the full representation of the entity to the Publisher service of Ellucian Ethos Integration (5). The Publisher service is responsible for publishing the change notification to the respective queues of Subscriber applications defined in the tenant's Configuration database. Non-authoritative applications that subscribe to change notifications for specific entities are responsible for polling the Message Queue service (6) to retrieve change notifications in their queue (the lines show the retrieval of queued messages by the consuming application).

Note: The arrows in the diagram depict the flow of data, not necessarily action on the part of components.

Install the Ellucian Messaging Service with Banner

The Ellucian Messaging Service is message queuing software that decouples the event generator for Banner or Colleague from the software that processes the business events.

It is recommended that the Messaging Service and Messaging Adapter be installed behind a firewall.

Note: If the Messaging Service and Messaging Adapter are installed a separate server from the ERP's Web API server, the recommended server configuration is a 2 core CPU with at least 2GB of memory.
Note:

If Erlang or RabbitMQ are already installed for a prior product, they should not be re-installed. Multiple Ellucian products can and should use the same RabbitMQ installation, but you can use different installations for production and non-production environments.

However, on the CRM application servers for CRM Recruit, Ellucian installs RabbitMQ separately from any other RabbitMQ installation to be used specifically for the Ellucian Task Service for Recruit. This is used separately from Banner Event Publisher or Ethos functionality, which is the recommended usage.

Install the Ellucian Messaging Service on Windows

If you are installing the Ellucian Messaging Service with a Windows operating system, perform this procedure to download the installer and install the components.

Before you begin

Before installing the Ellucian Messaging Service, determine the appropriate version for your implementation. See Identify Ethos Integration component versions for Banner.

If you have a previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service installed, you must uninstall it before installing a newer version. In addition, you must stop the RabbitMQ service using the Windows Services console.

Warning: Uninstalling the previous version will delete any existing message queues. Verify that all message queues are empty before uninstalling the previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service.
Warning: Uninstalling the previous version will delete the ssl directory and the rabbitmq.config file. If you have configured the previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service for SSL, you should backup these files before uninstalling the Ellucian Messaging Service.

Install the prerequisite Microsoft® package. Go to https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-160 and install C and C++ (MSVC) runtime libraries.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service executable file from the Ellucian Downloads or using SA Valet.

    The file is named EllucianMessagingServicexxxSetup.exe where xxx is the version number.

  2. As an administrator, run the EllucianMessagingServicexxxSetup.exe installer to launch the install wizard.
  3. Follow the wizard prompts. In the Base Configuration Information page of the wizard, enter the following values:
    Field Description Example
    Username Username of the RabbitMQ administrative user that will be created by the install. ellucian
    Password A password for that user. rabbit
    Virtual Host Name of the RabbitMQ virtual host that will be created by the install. bep_events_host

    Record the RabbitMQ username, password, and virtual host name in the Banner/Ethos Integration worksheet.

    When you set up the Banner Event Publisher and enter configuration settings in the BannerEventPublisher_configuration.groovy file, you must enter this same value in the virtualHostName setting.

Results

The installer will perform the following actions:
  • Install Erlang and RabbitMQ.
  • Enable the RabbitMQ admin UI.
  • Configure RabbitMQ for the specified admin user.
  • Create the indicated AMQP virtual host.
Install the Ellucian Messaging Service on Linux

If you are installing the Ellucian Messaging Service with a Linux operating system, perform this procedure to download the installer and install the components.

Before you begin

Before installing the Ellucian Messaging Service, determine the appropriate version for your implementation. See Identify Ethos Integration component versions for Banner.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Messaging Service that is certified with your Ethos API version. For the certified versions, see the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix or Banner Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    Ellucian provides a zip file for each supported Linux operating system. Download the file that matches your version of Linux.

    For example: Red Hat Linux 8 - EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip.

    To verify the version of Linux that is installed on the server, enter cat /etc/redhat-release.

    To verify the version of Ubuntu that is installed on the server, enter lsb_release -a.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ems.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command. Replace the EMS and Linux version numbers with the ones in your zip file.
    unzip EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip
    The extracted ZIP file will contain:
    • a ConfigureEMS shell script.
    • an Erlang RPM file.
    • a RabbitMQ RPM file.
  4. As root, install Erlang.
    For RHEL 8, enter the following commands:
    yum install erlang-23.3.4.11-1.el8.x86_64.rpm
    For Ubuntu 22.04, enter the following commands:
    dpkg -i esl-erlang_25.3.2-1~ubuntu~jammy_amd64.deb
    Note: If you receive an error that libsctp1 is a dependency, enter apt-get install libsctp1. After libsctp1 has been installed, re-run the erlang install command.
  5. As root, install RabbitMQ.
    For RHEL 8, enter the following command:
    yum install rabbitmq-server-3.9.1-1.el8.noarch.rpm
    Note: If you receive an error that socat is a dependency, enter yum install socat. After socat has been installed, re-run the RabbitMQ install command.

    For Ubuntu 22.04, enter the following commands: 

    dpkg -i rabbitmq-server_3.11.23-1_all.deb
  6. Configure AMQP and the Ellucian Messaging Service using the delivered ConfigureEMS shell script.
    1. Change permissions on the configuration script.
      chmod 700 ConfigureEMS
    2. As root, run the configuration script with its three required command line arguments.
      Syntax: ConfigureEMS username password vhostname
      Argument Description Example
      username Username of the RabbitMQ administrative user that will be created by the install. ellucian
      password A password for that user. rabbit
      vhostname Name of the RabbitMQ virtual host that will be created by the install. bep_events_host
      Example: ./ConfigureEMS ellucian rabbit bep_events_host

      Record the RabbitMQ username, password, and virtual host name in the Banner/Ethos Integration worksheet.

      When you set up the Banner Event Publisher and enter configuration settings in the BannerEventPublisher_configuration.groovy file, you must enter this same value in the virtualHostName setting.

Upgrade the Ellucian Messaging Service on Linux

If you have installed the with a Linux operating system, perform this procedure to upgrade it.

About this task

You may encounter errors when you upgrade because of version incompatibilities. Errors can occur when you upgrade EMS from version 7 to 8.

If you run into RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibility, and you want to preserve existing data and configuration, follow these steps Resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities when upgrading EMS.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Messaging Service that is certified with your Ethos API version. For the certified versions, see the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix or Banner Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    Ellucian provides a zip file for each supported Linux operating system. Download the file that matches your version of Linux.

    For example: Red Hat Linux 8 - EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip.

    To verify the version of Linux that is installed on the server, enter cat /etc/redhat-release.

    To verify the version of Ubuntu that is installed on the server, enter lsb_release -a.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ems.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command. Replace the EMS and RHEL version numbers with the numbers in your zip file.
    unzip EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip
    The extracted ZIP file will contain:
    • a ConfigureEMS shell script.
    • an Erlang RPM file.
    • a RabbitMQ RPM file.
  4. Stop the Banner Event Publisher (for Banner clients) or EDX (for Colleague clients).
    See the Banner or Colleague documentation for more information about stopping BEP or EDX.
  5. Stop the service with the following command. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
  6. As root, upgrade Erlang.
  7. As root, upgrade .
  8. Start the service with the following command. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
  9. Start BEP (for Banner clients) or EDX (for Colleague clients).
    See the Banner or Colleague documentation for more information about starting BEP or EDX.
Resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities when upgrading EMS

When you upgrade the Ellucian Messaging Service, resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities if they occur.

About this task

Errors can occur when you upgrade EMS from version 7 to 8. If you run into RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibility, and you want to preserve existing data and configuration, follow these steps.

Procedure

  1. Prepare a backup directory.
    1. Create a directory named backup under /home/ems. 
      sudo mkdir -p /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
    2. Set the RabbitMQ user as the owner of the directory and grant permissions to write. 
      sudo chown rabbitmq:rabbitmq /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
sudo chmod 755 /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
  2. Export RabbitMQ configurations, messages, and definitions.
    1. Before copying any data, stop the RabbitMQ server. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
    2. Copy the mnesia directory (messages db). 
      sudo cp -r /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/mnesia.bak
    3. Copy RabbitMQ configurations. 
      sudo cp -r /etc/rabbitmq /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/rabbitmq.bak
    4. Start the RabbitMQ server to copy definitions, then execute the command export_definitions. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl export_definitions /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/definitions.json
  3. Uninstall RabbitMQ and Erlang.
    1. Stop the RabbitMQ server, then delete RabbitMQ directories. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
sudo rm -rf /etc/rabbitmq /var/lib/rabbitmq
    2. Remove RabbitMQ and Erlang from the system. 
      sudo yum remove -y erlang rabbitmq-server
  4. Upgrade RabbitMQ and Erlang .
    1. Replace the RabbitMQ and Erlang RPMs with the files included in your zip file. 
      sudo yum install -y <erlang-rpm> <rabbitmq-server-rpm>
  5. Get the node name.
    It is necessary to obtain the RabbitMQ node name to configure the server after you import the previous RabbitMQ version.
    1. Start RabbitMQ.
    2. Get the server status, which includes the name of the node from the current server instance.
    3. Store the value to configure the server later. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl status | grep "Node name"
  6. Import RabbitMQ definitions.
    1. Run the import definitions command when the server is up.
      A message displays stating that the process is asynchronous and can take some time. Watch target node logs for completion.
    2. After completion, stop the server to continue with RabbitMQ backup import 
      sudo rabbitmqctl import_definitions /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/definitions.json
sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
  7. Import RabbitMQ configurations and messages.
    1. Create a copy of /etc/rabbitmq and /var/lib/rabbitmq before you import the configurations and messages backup in case something goes wrong.
    2. Remove /etc/rabbitmq, then copy the rabbitmq.bak directory content to /etc into a new RabbitMQ directory. 
      sudo rm -rf /etc/rabbitmq
sudo cp -r /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/rabbitmq.bak/. /etc/rabbitmq
    3. Do the same with the mnesia directory. After importing mnesia, set the RabbitMQ user as owner and grant permissions to write. 
      sudo rm -rf /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo cp -r /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/mnesia.bak/. /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo chown -R rabbitmq:rabbitmq /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo chmod 755 /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
      Before starting the RabbitMQ server, you must add feature flags to RabbitMQ to be able to start the server successfully. Edit the file /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia/<rabbitmq-node-name>-feature_flags and add the following to the array.
      stream_filtering,message_containers,stream_update_config_command
  8. Start RabbitMQ.
    1. After all imports are done, start RabbitMQ server and verify it starts up.
    2. Enable all stable feature flags to prevent unexpected behavior. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl enable_feature_flag all
Configure RabbitMQ for SSL (Windows)

Install the SSL certificate, private key, and CA certificate files required to configure RabbitMQ for SSL on Windows. After performing these steps, a secure port will be set up that will accept AMQPS communications.

Before you begin

You must have three certificates files from a well-known Certificate Authority.

  • Private Key (should not be password protected)
  • Root + Intermediate Certificates
  • Server Certificate

Any intermediate certificates need to be contained in the same file as the root certificate. The server certificate should be in its own file. All of the certificate files, including the key, should be in a Base64 encoded (PEM) format. If you view them in a text editor, the file should begin and end with Begin Certificate and End Certificate or Begin RSA Private Key and End RSA Private Key.

Procedure

  1. Create an ssl directory under the installation directory to store the certificate files.

    For example, C:\Program Files\Ellucian\EllucianMessagingService\AMQP\rabbitmq_server-x.x.x\ssl

  2. Copy the two certificate files and one key file into the ssl directory.
  3. Create or edit the file: %APPDATA%\Roaming\RABBITMQ\advanced.config
  4. Add the following to the file, using the appropriate certificate names.
    Note: Backslashes ("\") in the configuration file are interpreted as an escape character. You must use "\\" or "/" when specifying file paths.
    [
  {rabbit, [
     {ssl_listeners, [5671]}, 
     {ssl_options, [{cacertfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/root_cert.pem"}, 
     {certfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/server_cert.pem"}, 
     {keyfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/key.pem"},
     {verify,verify_peer},
     {fail_if_no_peer_cert,false}]}
]}
].
    Warning: Make sure to include a period (.) at the end of the code snippet. This period must be present.
  5. Go to the Windows Services by running services.msc. Scroll down to the RabbitMQ service, and stop the service.
  6. Click Start > All Programs > RabbitMQ > (Re)install Service.
  7. Go to the Windows Services by running services.msc. Scroll down to the RabbitMQ service, and start the service.
Configure RabbitMQ for SSL (Linux)

Install the SSL certificate, private key, and CA certificate files required to configure RabbitMQ for SSL on Linux. After performing these steps, a secure port will be set up that will accept AMQPS communications.

Before you begin

You must have three certificates files from a well-known Certificate Authority.

  • Private Key (should not be password protected)
  • Root + Intermediate Certificates
  • Server Certificate

Any intermediate certificates need to be contained in the same file as the root certificate. The server certificate should be in its own file. All of the certificate files, including the key, should be in a Base64 encoded (PEM) format. If you view them in a text editor, the file should begin and end with Begin Certificate and End Certificate or Begin RSA Private Key and End RSA Private Key.

Procedure

  1. Create an ssl directory under /etc/rabbitmq to store the certificate files.
  2. Copy the two certificate files and the one key file into the ssl directory.
  3. Create or edit the file /etc/rabbitmq/advanced.config.
  4. Add the following entries to the file, using the appropriate certificate file names. 
    [
  {rabbit, [
     {ssl_listeners, [5671]},
     {ssl_options, [
       {cacertfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/root_cert.pem"},
       {certfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/server_cert.pem"},
       {keyfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/key.pem"},
       {verify,verify_peer},
       {fail_if_no_peer_cert,false}
    ]}
  ]}
].
    Warning: Make sure to include a period (.) at the end of the code snippet. This period must be present.
  5. Restart the RabbitMQ service by running the following commands. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
/sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
Validate the Ellucian Messaging Service

You can use the RabbitMQ administrative interface to check that the Ellucian Messaging Service is correctly configured for Ethos Integration.

Procedure

  1. In a browser, navigate to port 15672 on the server where you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    Examples: http://localhost:15672 (from the Ellucian Messaging Service server) or http://ems.mycollege.edu:15672 (from another computer in the network)
    The URL starts with http rather than https, as shown in the examples. When you configured RabbitMQ for SSL, you secured the amqp connection, not the RabbitMQ administrative interface.
  2. At the login prompt, enter the username and password that you specified when you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    Example: Username = ellucian, password = rabbit
  3. On the Overview page, in the Listening Ports section, check that the table includes amqp::5672 and amqp/ssl::5671.
  4. Click the Admin tab, and then select Virtual Hosts.
  5. On the Virtual Hosts page, check the following:
    • The table should include a row for the virtual host whose name you specified when you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    • The Users column should show that the user created during the Ellucian Messaging Service install has access to that virtual host. Example: ellucian
  6. If either the virtual host or user does not exist, you can create them:
    1. If the virtual host does not exist, click Virtual Hosts on the Admin page, and then select Add a new virtual host.
    2. If the user does not exist, click Users on the Admin page, and then select Add a user.
    3. After creating the virtual host or user, grant that user permissions on the virtual host:
      • On the Users page, click on the username to access the Permissions page.
      • Set the default .* permissions for configure, write, and read access.

Generate Banner GUIDs

The Banner Ethos APIs enable you to interact with multiple non-Banner systems.

Before initiating Banner Ethos API integration, you must generate the Globally Unique Identifiers (GUID) associated with each resource (persons, section-registrations, and so on).

This section will assist you to perform the tasks required before GUID generation can begin and then the actual GUID generation process itself.

Note: Banner Operational Data Store (ODS) customers should stop ODS incremental processes during a GURGUID run, and do a full ODS reload after completion of the GURGUID process.
GUID definition

A GUID is a unique string of 36 characters.

The BANSECR.GOKGUID.get_uuid function generates Banner GUIDs and in the following format.

xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-zxxx-
xxxxxxxxxxxx
This format represents the value of the GUID as lowercase hexadecimal digits in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4, and 12 digits, separated by dashes. In this format:
  • x = any lowercase hexadecimal digit.
  • 4 = the digit 4.
  • z = 8, 9, a, or b.

For example, e39bddad-386f-49ed-be63-54f7265de42b.

Note: Ellucian RESTful APIs GUID conforms to the version 4 of RFC 4122 as identified in the above format. The JSON schema definitions constrain GUID format. The GUID format cannot be changed.
Banner Ethos identifies GUIDs for each resource (that is persons, section, course, and so on.) and stores those values in one of three locations.
  • The table itself (for example, GORVISA)
  • A shadow table (for example, SHRTNID)
  • The GORGUID table
Prepare for GUID generation

Familiarize yourself with the following procedure in preparation for generating Banner Ethos GUIDs.

About this task

Warning: Review your custom triggers before executing the GURGUID job. As GURGUID adds a GUID column to many key tables and then updates it (touching what could be millions of records), institutions need to be aware that triggers on these tables will fire for all of these updated records. If your custom triggers are not specific enough in your :OLD and :NEW comparisons (or the comparison is to activity date, which is not updated), this can result in unintentional code execution. The use of shadow tables on more significant tables (such as sarappd, shrttrm, sarchkl, sgbstdn) instead of adding a column to them is preferable.

Procedure

  1. Review the Ellucian Customer Center article: 000043988 – Understanding Ethos GUIDs in Banner.
    This article gives detailed information about GUIDs, GUID generation, and troubleshooting techniques in addition to describing GUID usage with regards to the Ethos APIs. To resolve issues while generating GUIDs, see Common Problems and Resolutions within that document.
  2. Assign the appropriate users to the jobs listed in the subsequent sections of this document.
    Note: You will need to review the nature of the jobs below and assign the super users to the objects directly or to the class. These jobs are reserved for those users who have a technical knowledge of the system and understand the ramifications of running these types of infrastructure jobs. For more information about granting access, see Security maintenance (GSASECR).
  3. Synchronize the BAN_DEFAULT_GUIDGEN_M class after assigning security access.
    There is a new role, BAN_DEFAULT_GUIDGEN_M, that is associated with each of these objects. You will notice on the GSASECR / Classes tab that the class may be Out of Sync after assigning new users to the class. Click the Synchronize or Synchronize All button on the GSASECR / Classes tab to ensure that after the class has been assigned to users, the roles are properly granted.
    Note: If you do not synchronize the class, you may see a Role Not Granted error when trying to run the jobs.
    The Banner Ethos API upgrade process adds a GUID column to many key tables. Running of GURGUID updates the GUID column, impacting potentially millions of records. You should be aware that triggers on these tables will fire for all of these updated records. If your custom triggers are not specific enough in their :OLD and :NEW comparisons, or if the comparison is to activity date, which is not update, this can result in unintentional code execution.
  4. Use the Process Submission Controls (GJAPCTL) page to run the GUID generation (GURGUID) process in report mode.


    This will provide a report of the status of your Banner tables with respect to GUID generation without generating any GUIDs or making any changes. This will provide a snapshot of information before running GUID generation.

    1. Select the GURGUID job submission process.
    2. Set the GUID generation method to the value N for Do not generate GUIDs; Report Only.
    3. Set Modules for GUID generation to %.
    4. Submit the GURGUID process.
    5. Review the resulting report.
  5. Run database statistics as per the GURGUID report, if needed. This will enable better performance of the GUID generation process.
  6. Optional: Estimate new storage requirements through the guid_sizing_estimates.sql script described in the Ellucian Customer Center Article: 000043988 mentioned above.
  7. Run the Ethos Diagnostics (GUREDIA) process. This process should be run to perform a diagnostic check of data used within Ethos.

    Each of the parameters has a Y or N option to enable specific checks to be run or bypassed.

    Note: The diagnostics should be run one time with all options set to Y to gain an overall understanding of the environment.
    Parameter Values Description
    help Y or N More complete description about each parameter.
    versions Y or N Database and product version information.
    goriccr Y or N GORICCR validation checks.
    sections Y or N Verification that the Status and Duration codes being used are mapped in GORICCR
    addresses Y or N Verification that nation ISO codes exist for Address types being used.
    instructional-events Y or N Verification that building definitions used for instructional events are defined.
    persons Y or N Verification of gender codes, ISO codes for nations and currency, and a list of unmapped values for e-mail types, address types, telephone types, and marital status codes.
    recruitment Y or N Verification that the Checklist codes being used are mapped in GORICCR.
    section-registration-status Y or N Verification that the Registration Status codes being used are mapped in GORICCR to the correct STVRSTS Status type.
    API User to Validate security resources User ID Verification that the correct security rules are in place for this user.
    Note: If you leave this parameter null, the check will be bypassed.
    security-checks Y or N Analysis of security checks for API user, listing Banner Users authorized to access at least one API, and listing Banner Users with at least one active API masking rule defined.
    Note: In a typical environment, access to the APIs should be limited to a small number of users.
    api-access Y or N List of users with access to the APIs, the type of access, and any API masking rules defined.
    registration-history Y or N Verification that Registration History tables are in sync.
  8. Correct SHRGRID Grade Errors (SURGRID) if the Student application is installed.
    1. Run the SURGRID process to check for registration history grade GUIDs that are not in sync.
    2. Specify the parameters for this process as follows:
      Parameter Description
      Update or Audit The SURGRID process can be run in Audit mode to report orphaned SHRGRID records. If any orphan records are found, the process should be run in Update mode to delete those orphans and insert new SHRGRID records as needed for the affected registrations.
      START TERM This parameter will identify or fix SHRGRID records for that term and all subsequent terms.
Job submission processes

There are several Ethos related job submission processes.

The following jobs are defined as part of the menu item Ethos Administrative Jobs (*GENETHOS), which is under the System Functions or Administration (*GENSYS) menu under the General (*GENERAL) menu.

Job submission processes associated with GUID generation

  • GURGUDR: Summary of the GUID generation status
  • GURGUID: GUID generation for Banner Ethos API
  • GURGDJK: Kill or Report GUID generation jobs for Banner Ethos API
  • GURGDTC: Disable Triggers and Constraints for Banner Ethos API
  • GUADUPS: Find and Fix Duplicate Surrogate IDs
  • GUAORPH: Find and Fix orphaned and missing GUID records
  • GUREDIA: Ethos Diagnostics

Job submission processes not associated with GUID generation

  • GUABEPR: Report for Banner Event Processing (BEP) Events
  • GUABEPT: List Disabled BEP Events and Disable the Associated Triggers
  • GUAMEPA: Report on the MEP status of all tables
If you have the Student Product you will also see three jobs under the *STUETHOS menu (Ethos Administrative Jobs for Student), which is under the *STDADMIN (Student Administration) menu.
  • SURSSDE – Create SDE rule for SOAORUL dates.
  • SURGRID – Process to correct grade errors in SHRGRID.
  • SHRDGPA – Calculate GPAs for all earned degrees and store the results in SHRDGMRS.

All Ethos job submission jobs have been assigned to a new class, BAN_ETHOS_C. Due to the nature of these jobs no user has been assigned access to the jobs with a direct grant or through the BAN_ETHOS_C class. You will have to assign access for applicable users using Banner security.

Preparations for GUID generation if you are interfacing with Elevate

Additional information about the process that will create a Supplemental Data Rule (SDE) entry for the SOBODTE table to store two new values used for Elevate processing—First Registration Date Override and Last Registration Date Override.

The systems will use these values as the First Registration Date and Last Registration Date when creating sections through Ethos Integration.

Note: This job does not require any parameters.

The SDE rule enables the entry of the override dates on SOAORUL as shown here.



Preparations for GUID generation in a MEP environment

Run the Find Duplicate Surrogate IDs process (GUADUPS), which scans all tables under MEP that have a SURROGATE ID and identifies any duplicates that are found.

About this task

In some cases, data may have been replicated in a MEP environment by cloning values from one MEP code to another. Depending on the process used, the TABLE_NAME_SURROGATE_ID may have been replicated as well.

Because the surrogate ID is often the link between a parent table and its shadow GUID table, it is best to ensure that surrogate id values are always unique.

Procedure

  1. Go to the GUADUPS job submission page.
  2. Specify the following parameters for the GUADUPS process:
    1. Enter the Update or Audit option.
      The valid values are as follows:
      Value Description
      A Audit potential changes and indicate what would occur if the Update option were selected. You should execute first in the Audit mode and then review the results before setting it to U to make the update.
      U Update the duplicate surrogate IDs with a new unique value to ensure that they are unique going forward.
    2. Enter the Max Duplicates option.
      • GUADUPS will scan all MEPed tables that have a <table_name>_SURROGATE_ID and identify any duplicates that are found.
      • This value will represent the number of duplicates, which would be listed in the report. 0 indicates all duplicates should be listed.
      • All duplicates, whether printed or not, will be processed.
    3. Enter the Force Re-execution (Y or N) option.
      Typically, this report only needs to be executed one time and therefore the Force Re-execution option must be specified as well because it can be a very long running process. The valid values are as follows:
      Value Description
      Y Verify the duplicates again even though the process has already been executed.
      N Do not execute if the process has already been run.
      Note: If the job is already executed, a row in GURTRCK with GURTRCK_OBJECT_NAME set to CHECK_DUPLICATE_SURROGATE_IDS will be present.
Run the GUID Generation process (GURGUID)

The general recommendations for running GUID generation as required by Banner Ethos APIs.

About this task

Note: It is imperative that the GURGUID process be run following each Ethos Upgrade or Installation.
Warning: Review your custom triggers before executing the GURGUID job. As GURGUID adds a GUID column to many key tables and then updates it (touching what could be millions of records), institutions need to be aware that triggers on these tables will fire for all of these updated records. If your custom triggers are not specific enough in your :OLD and :NEW comparisons (or the comparison is to activity date, which is not updated), this can result in unintentional code execution. The use of shadow tables on more significant tables (such as sarappd, shrttrm, sarchkl, sgbstdn) instead of adding a column to them is preferable.

Procedure

  1. Use the Process Submission Controls (GJAPCTL) page and run the GUID generation (GURGUID) process with the required parameters.
  2. Optional: Run GURGUDR (or GURGUID in report mode) to check the progress of the GUID generation (GURGUID) process.
    No parameters exist for GURGUDR.
  3. Optional: Run GURGDJK to kill GURGUID as needed according to your schedule.

    The GURGUID process was designed to be started and stopped as needed and does not have to run to completion after the initial start.

  4. Repeat the above steps until GUID generation (GURGUID) is complete.
    The following figure shows the recommended GUID generation flowchart:

GURGUID parameters

The GURGUID process creates GUIDs as needed.

Note: It is imperative that the GURGUID process be run following each Ethos Upgrade or Installation.

The following are parameters for the GURGUID process:

Enter GUID generation method

This value relates directly to the type of job as specified in GURTRCK. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description Notes
S Serial Most tables are processed using the serial method.
Always use the serial method to process shadow tables:
  • Shadow tables including GORGUID have many rows.
  • If the shadow table in GURTRCK is marked as parallel, the job will only be picked up if the parameter indicates parallel; however, the actual generation will still be processed using SERIAL method
P Parallel
  • Use the parallel method to process non-shadow tables with many rows that have the GUID column residing in them.
  • Use the parallel method to run the multiple jobs (based on the number of parallel threads defined in GUREOPT) spawned through DBMS_SCHEDULER, and if the total number of rows in the table exceeds the parallel threshold.
% Run both Parallel and Serial type jobs (suggested value).  
N Do not generate any GUIDs, and only report on the status.  

Modules for GUID generation

The process can be run for a single module or for multiple modules by duplicating the record. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
F Finance
G General
N Position Control
P Payroll
R Financial Aid
S Student
T Accounts Receivable
% All modules (Suggested value)

Debug Y or N

In most cases, there is no need to specify that the report be run in Debug mode, but if needed specify a value of Y. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
N Do not generate additional debug messages (suggested value).
Y Generate additional debug messages if errors are found during the process.

Print status (Y or N)

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
N Do not print GUID status before or after execution.
P Print the GUID status but not the trigger information.
U Print the status for unprocessed GUIDs (that is NOT_PROCESSED, ERROR, BYPASS).
Y Print all GUID status and trigger information (suggested value).

Maximum Parallel Threads

Use this parameter to override and update the values defined in GUREOPT for parallel processing. If left blank, use the current values (suggested value - blank).

Parallel row count threshold

Use this parameter to override and update the values defined in GUREOPT for parallel processing. If left blank, use the current values (suggested value - blank).

Gen GUIDs for Individual Tables

This parameter gives you the ability to indicate specific tables for which GUIDs should be generated. You may enter as many tables as required, or none. If entered, the GUID Generation Method and Module parameters are ignored, meaning you can mix and match products and methods (suggested value - blank).

Force GUID Generation

This parameter gives you the ability to force processing of the selected tables. If a GUID already exists, no action will be taken. If GUIDs are missing, they will be generated. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Force a re-generation regardless of GURTRCK status.
N Only process GUIDs if the GURTRCK indicator is NOT_PROCESSED or ERROR (suggested value).

Force disabling of BEP trigger

This parameter gives you the ability to disable BEP triggers for the table for which you are generating GUIDs.

Note: This should only be done if you are not live with Ethos Integration. Typically, the initial generation of GUIDs means that integrations are not yet in place, however you may have non-Ethos Integration using BEP triggers as well.

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Force the BEP trigger defined in GURTRCK to be disabled.
N Leave the BEP trigger as defined in GURTRCK.
Differences between the GURGUID process and standard Banner processes

Different aspects of GURGUID when compared to typical Banner processes.

  • GURGUID does not produce the typical .lis file. GURGUID updates GUROUTP with the report output and optional debug.log. This output is available through GJIREVO as the process is running. The prefix {InProcess} indicates that the process is still running, but you can view the information before the job completes.

  • GURGUID uses DBMS_SCHEDULER to process the GUID generation.
    • By using DBMS_SCHEDULER, it appears as though GURGUID has completed, while it is still processing in the background.
      • You can use the GUID Generation Method = N in GURGUID to get a status report.
      • You can also use the GURGUDR (GUID GEN Report) to report the status.
    • Because the GURGUID job will finish execution after it has spawned the jobs to the scheduler, the .lis file will contain minimal information (that is the date, time, and parameters). In order to produce a .lis file (or PDF) for the complete output, you must execute GUROUTF. For more information about this process, see Output file generation (GUROUTF).
      Note: As of 9.16, the GUROUTF process is automatically executed at the end of processing so there is no longer the need to run it manually.
  • The GURTRCK table keeps track of progress and status for each table. You can submit multiple executions of GURGUID. Each new process will look at GURTRCK and start with the next table that requires processing.
  • GURGUID will commit after each table. For large tables, commits will be performed after 5,000 operations.
  • GURGUID can be stopped and restarted whenever it is needed. For more information about reporting or terminating GURGUID processes, see Report, terminate, or purge the GURGUID process (GURGDJK).
Run multiple GURGUID jobs

It is possible to submit the GURGUID job multiple times; one-time for each module, or one job to perform all modules.

Running GURGUID multiple times will decrease the overall elapsed time for completing the jobs. The GURTRCK table keeps track of what processes have not yet run, which ones are in progress, and which ones have completed successfully. If you run the job multiple times, there is no concern for re-processing an individual table.

Limitations while running GURGUID

It is recommended that you do not run multiple Banner update batch jobs on the same table at the same time, regardless of the actual process, because of potential errors with row deadlocking.

Due to limitations in Banner, running multiple Banner update batch jobs on the same table at the same time could lead to errors which will terminate the batch jobs. Operations from INB, Banner Admin page, or Self-Service during a Banner update batch job are less likely to generate errors because updates are usually made for a single row of data. If an error does occur, resubmitting the INB form, Banner Admin page, or Self-Service page should work.

Run the GUID generation Status Report (GURGUDR)

Use GURGUDR process to report on the progress of GUID generation.

Because the GURGUID can be a long-running process, a separate Banner job, GURGUDR, can be run to report on the progress of GUID generation. The GURGUDR process queries the GURTRCK table to report on which tables GURGUID have completed the GUID generation and which ones are not yet processed. The report will provide a list of tables eligible for GUID generation and their status. At the end of the report, it will also display an overall percent complete for GURGUID.

The GURGUDR process can be run while GURGUID is also running or it can be run at any other time.

Note: No parameters are required for this job.
Report, terminate, or purge the GURGUID process (GURGDJK)

You can run GURGDJK to terminate the GURGUID process.

About this task

Because the GURGUID process can be a long-running process, it can be terminated, and processing can be continued later according to your schedule.
Note: If you cancel a job in the middle of the process, work completed up to that point will be committed.

GURGDJK will terminate all GURGUID jobs running in the Oracle DBMS Scheduler, in addition to any jobs that have been scheduled to run but are not yet running.

Procedure

  1. Go to the GURGDJK job submission page.
  2. Specify the following parameters for the GURGDJK process:
    1. Report or Kill Jobs.
      The valid values are as follows:
      Value Description
      R Report the status of GURGUID jobs.
      K Report the status of GURGUID jobs and kill any that are executing.
    2. Report History.
      The valid values are as follows:
      Value Description
      Y Report the history of all GURGUID jobs in ALL_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS.
      N Do not report any history.
    3. Purge jobs older than days.
      The valid values are as follows:
      Value Description
      0 Purge all jobs.
      999 Do not purge any jobs.
      001-998 Purge jobs that are older than this number of days.
Optional processes

You can run the additional processes on an as needed basis.

Calculate Degree GPAs (SHRDGPA)

Use this process to calculate and store the Degree GPAs for all earned degrees.

The API for student-grade-point-averages, will return earned degree GPAs and associated hours, which are not stored in Banner.

This process will calculate and store the Degree GPAs in the new SHRDGMRS table for all earned degrees; because to calculate them from within the API would be a huge performance issue. At this time, only earned degrees are included in the model.

The following are the parameters for this process:

Parameter Description
START_TERM This parameter will have one value. It is an optional field.
END_TERM This parameter will have one value. It is an optional field.
STUDENT_ID This parameter will have multiple values. It is an optional field.
Note: Either START_TERM and END_TERM, or a STUDENT_ID, is required for the job to run.

Users will run this process for a term range to initially populate the table. Because the process may take a long time to run when you have been using Banner for several years, you may want to run it more than one time to populate the table.

Example: You may run this process for 199710-200440, from 200510-201240, and then again for 201310- <current-term>.

This process should become a part of normal end-of-term processing, after grades have been rolled and degrees have been awarded, so that records can be added to SHRDGMRS for newly earned degrees, and updated for existing degrees if needed. For end-of-term processing, START_TERM and END_TERM could be set to the same value. Example: 201840-201840.

Because you can use various fields to capture the term in which the degree was awarded or not capture it at all, the following hierarchy will be used for finding the term of the degree. The last field is a required field.

  • SHRDGMR_TERM_CODE_GRAD
  • SHRDGMR_TERM_CODE_COMP
  • SHRDGMR_TERM_CODE_STUREC

Only earned degrees will be considered, means SHRDGMR_DEGS_CODE must have a value, where STVDEGS_AWARD_STATUS_IND = A (where A stands for Awarded).

Find and delete orphaned GUID rows in shadow tables (GUAORPH)

Use GUAORPH process to find any GUID rows are orphans.

This process is used to find any GUID rows that are orphans, that is, those that cannot relate back to a parent, and optionally delete those rows. This may be due to manual SQL manipulations of tables, PIDM Merges, or incorrect conversion processes.

This report should only be run after GUID generation has completed, otherwise the number of missing GUIDs would be excessive and misleading.

The following are parameters for the GUAORPH process:

Update or Audit

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description Notes
A Audit Report on the changes that will be made. Review the results before running in Update mode.
U Update Delete orphaned GUIDs. If missing GUIDs were reported, set the Execute GURGUID parameter to Y to generate them.

Max detail to print

  • Specify the maximum number of detailed error messages to display.
  • A value of 0 indicates that all errors should display. Typically, a value of 10 or 20 will be enough to give you an idea of any issues.

DEBUG (Y or N)

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Display the SQL used to find and delete the orphans.
N Do not display the SQL.

This is the recommended value.

GORGUID Verification

Because there are approximately 50 tables associated with GORGUID, you can specify that ALL, NONE, or an OVERRIDE list of parent tables should be processed. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
ALL Verify all tables are related to GORGUID.
NONE Bypass validation for all tables related to GORGUID.
OVERRIDE Only process those tables listed in the Override GORGUID resources option.

Override GORGUID Resources

If OVERRIDE was selected for GORGUID Verification, select any of the options provided in the drop-down list for this parameter.

You may duplicate this row as many times as needed to indicate one or more resources to be processed.

Shadow Table Verification

Because there are several different shadow tables, you can specify that ALL, NONE, or an OVERRIDE list of tables should be processed. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
ALL Verify all shadow tables.
NONE Bypass validation for all shadow tables.
OVERRIDE Only process those tables listed in the Override Shadow Tables option.

Override Shadow Tables

If OVERRIDE was selected for Shadow Table Verification, select any of the options provided in the drop-down list for this parameter.

You may duplicate this row as many times as needed to indicate one or more shadow tables to be processed.

Check for orphaned GUIDs

You can choose whether you would like to check for orphaned GUIDs. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Check for orphans.
N Do not check for orphans.

Check for missing GUIDs

You can choose whether you would like to check for missing GUIDs, typically what GURGUID would generate. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Check for missing GUIDs.
N Do not check for missing GUIDs.

Execute GURGUID (Y or N)

While running GUAORPH, you can now automatically run GURGUID. If you ran GUAORPH in an UPDATE mode, the tables affected would be passed to GURGUID to run that process. The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Automatically submit GURGUID.
N Do not submit GURGUID.
Note: If you run a process referred to as PIDM Merge or perform direct SQL updates of Banner records (that is, processes outside the standard Banner processes) that deal specifically with the updating of primary keys or surrogate IDs for records.

You can perform the following actions after the updates:

  • Create the proper GUID rows, especially if the GUIDs are in a shadow table or GORGUID.
  • Issue appropriate BEP transactions to indicate the deletion of the old GUID or primary key and the creation of a new GUID or primary key.
  • Run GUAORPH followed by GURGUID to identify or fix orphaned records caused by the new primary key or GUID, or surrogate id combinations.
  • Typically, if you delete and add a row instead of changing the primary key or surrogate id directly, this will not be an issue.
Report BEP Events (GUABEPR)

GUABEPR process will allow you to report all information on all or selected BEP events.

The following are parameters for the GUABEPR process:

Enter the Event Names option

Enter the name (wild cards allowed) of the events that you want to report. All Ethos events have the format: EEDM.<product>.<resource identifier>.<primary table>.

Example: EEDM.GEN.Persons.GOREMAL or EEDM.STU.Subject.STVSUBJ

Enter the Print Internal IDs option

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Print the BEP internal IDs. This is only used for debugging.
N Do not print the internal IDs.

This is the recommended value.
MEP analysis report (GUAMEPA)

GUAMEPA process analyzes and reports on the overall MEP environment including, triggers, policies, and non-valid MEP codes identifying any potential discrepancies.

The following are parameters for the GUAMEPA process:

Report Type

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
FULL List all relevant information along with any errors found.
ERROR List only the errors.

Count Rows per MEP code

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y Count the number of rows per MEP code and per table.
  • If this option is selected, any rows with a VPDI_CODE value not found in GTVVPDI will also be diagnosed.
  • Depending on the size of tables, enabling this option will significantly increase execution time.
N Do not count rows per MEP code.

Create "fixes" script

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y If errors are found because of missing triggers or policies, a fix it script will be created with the necessary SQL to fix these issues.
N Do not create a fix it script.
Note: The fix it SQL is not executed by this process and will have to be executed by a DBA after reviewing the contents and backing up as needed.

Create OWNER policy

The valid values are as follows:

Value Description
Y If the OWNER and ALL policies are NULL, an additional component will be added to the fix it script that will set the OWNER Policy to SUID.
N No additional policy changes will be generated.

Additional Schema Owners

The row can be replicated as many times as needed to specify any additional schemas that need to be analyzed in addition to the default set of schemas that will be processed. Those default schemas are as follows:

ALUMNI, BANIDM, BANIMGR, BANINST1, BANSECR, BWAMGR, BWFMGR, BWGMGR, BWLMGR, BWPMGR, BWRMGR, BWSMGR, FAISMGR, FIMSMGR, FLEXREG, FTAEMGR, GENERAL, NLSUSER, OTGMGR, PAYROLL, POSNCTL, SATURN, STREAMSADMIN, TAISMGR, WFBANNER, and WTAILOR

Output file generation (GUROUTF)

GUROUTF process will extract report files from GUROUTP into the respective file in the file system.

GUROUTF is basically the opposite of GURINSO. All the Banner Ethos jobs that are part of Job Submission write their output directly to GUROUTP and are automatically available for viewing on GJIREVO.

Standard Banner jobs write the .lis and .log files and then (if a Printer designation of DATABASE was specified on GJAPCTL) those files will be copied to GUROUTP for viewing on GJIREVO.

The GUROUTF job will automatically execute with all jobs defined as part of the Ethos Job Submission. This means that those jobs will produce a .lis file, unless overridden in GTVSDAX. For more information about GTVSDAX, see GTVSDAX.

There may be instances where a .lis file was not created and you now want to create it. This can be done by manually executing GUROUTF.

The only parameter required is the one up number of the job for which the files should be extracted.

Note: If you are not authorized, through Banner security to a job for which you are attempting to extract files, your request will be denied.

Banner General 8.9.3 released GJRJLIS, a process that converts a file to a PDF. The file must exist on the file system and must be specified as an input parameter into this process. In order to enable this functionality for an Ethos job, the .lis file must be created through GUROUTF if it does not already exist.

GTVSDAX

If no .lis or .log file is desired, the automatic creation of these files can be controlled through GTVSDAX entries.

The GTVSDAX configurations for Ethos processes are defined in the ETHOS_JOBSUB GTVSDAX group. These are all enabled by default to write the report files to the file system for the given Ethos Job Sub process. If output files for any Ethos Job Sub process is not desired, the ETHOS_JOBSUB configurations can be set to N in GTVSDAX to prevent GUROUTF from writing the files to the file system.

Note: The GTVSDAX entries are ignored if you run GUROUTF manually through GJAPCTL.

The GTVSDAX settings are as follows:

Parameter Description
CODE The Ethos Job Sub process name.

Example: GURGUID
GROUP Must equal ETHOS_JOBSUB.
SEQUENCE Must be NULL or Blank.
EXTERNAL CODE Y or N to indicate whether the .lis and .log files are automatically created when the job is running.

Any other value or a missing entry is equivalent to a value of N.

Set up Banner in Ethos Integration

In Ethos Integration, create the Ethos applications for Banner and add the resources for which Banner is authoritative.

These steps are required for the Banner Integration, Banner Student, and Banner Business Process APIs.

Ethos Integration supports both Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) Banner implementations and non-MEP (single instance) implementations. The procedures for creating applications, assigning resources, and setting up other applications to access Banner resources, are different for non-MEP and MEP implementations, and are shown separately.

For a Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation of Banner, the recommended configuration in Ethos involves set up steps across multiple tenants. See Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (MEP - multiple tenants).

Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (non-MEP)

For a Banner single-entity (non-MEP) implementation, create the Ethos applications and add the resources for which Banner is authoritative.

Note: For a Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation of Banner, see Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (MEP - single tenant).
Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (non-MEP)

The Ethos Integration application records contain basic information about Banner, including the location of the Banner Student, Integration, and Business Process APIs, the resources for which Banner is the authoritative source, and the API key.

About this task

Perform this procedure three times, to create one application for the Banner Student API, one for the Banner Integration API, and one for the Banner Business Process API.

The Application Setup Wizard automatically adds ownership of Ethos resources to the application. It will get the list of resources to add by calling the /resources endpoint of the API.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, in the Create New App area, select From Catalog.
    The Browse Catalog page displays.
  4. On the Browse Catalog page, search for and select the Ellucian Banner application and select Create App.
    The catalog populates the resources owned by Banner.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.

    Examples: Banner Student API, Banner Integration API, or Banner Business Process API
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. On the Select Catalog Application page of the wizard, enter the following information and click Next:
    Field Entry
    Designated Owner of Shared Data Leave this check box unselected, as this application is not used for shared resources.
    Base URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Student API.

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Integration API.

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminBPAPI/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Business Process API.

    Base QAPI URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/qapi

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/qapi

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminAPI/qapi

    Username/Password Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API. See Define user privileges for API access.
  7. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    Banner does not subscribe to changes published by other Ethos applications.
  8. Optional: On the Finish page of the wizard, to unrestrict the restricted API key you created:
    1. Click Edit your new API key to allow IP access.
      The Edit API Key page displays. By default, Set API key to have IP address restrictions is selected.
    2. To add an IP address that is not restricted, enter the CIDR block for the Source IP Address.
    3. To add multiple IP addresses, enter a comma-separated list of IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks that are allowed to use the API key.
      When you make an API key available for use for one or multiple Ellucian products, use the following IP addresses:
         
      Ellucian Experience Experience domains and IP addresses
      Intelligent Learning Platform ILP domains and IP addresses
      Ellucian Workflow Ellucian Workflow NAT gateway IP addresses
      Ethos Data Connect Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses
    4. Click Save.
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure application-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the application now and configure settings later.
Update resources owned by Banner after an Ethos API upgrade (non-MEP)

Update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to resources owned by Banner that resulted from a new version of the Banner Ethos APIs.

About this task

When you originally created the applications for Banner, you added the resources that Banner owns. A new version of the Banner Ethos APIs can include changes to the resources owned by Banner. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to the resources owned by Banner.

Perform this procedure for each Ethos application that you created for Banner Ethos APIs.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the Banner application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. Click Auto-Configure Resources.
  6. In the Request Resources from Application window, enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API.
  7. Click Next.
    The list of resources owned by Banner is automatically updated to reflect changes in the new version of the APIs.
  8. Click Close.
Enable events associated with Banner-owned resources

Enable events associated with resources that are owned by Banner on the Applications page or the Resources page.

About this task

This feature will only work if a user has installed the following versions (or later) of Banner APIs:
  • Banner Integration API 9.37 (March 2025)
  • Banner Student API 9.37 (March 2025)
  • Banner Event Publisher 9.14 (March 2024)
Enable events associated with Banner-owned resources from the Applications tab

Update the Ethos applications for Banner with any events that are associated with resources that are owned by Banner.

Before you begin

  • Upgrade to the latest Banner version.
  • The event-configurations API must be installed on the Banner environment for these features to be available. See event-configurations.
  • To install an API in Banner, see Install Banner Ethos API.
  • Also see Set up the Banner Ethos APIs and supporting Banner software.

About this task

When you originally created the Ethos applications for Banner, you added the resources that Banner owns. A new version of the Banner Ethos APIs can include events that are associated with the resources owned by Banner. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos applications for Banner with any events to Banner owned resources.

Perform this procedure for each Ethos application that you created for Banner Ethos APIs.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the Banner application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
  5. Locate the resource in the Resource column for which you want to enable events. If necessary, enter the resource name in the Search Resources field to locate it.
  6. On the resource that has the ability to configure events, click More and then select Configure Events.
    The Events page displays for the selected resource.
  7. Optional: The Configure Events option displays only if the default resource owner has the ability to set up events.

    If the Configure Events option does not display in the menu, the event-configurations API is probably not in the Banner environment for that resource.

    Click the edit button in the Resource Owner column for the resource, select the correct environment, and click Confirm.

  8. Your Events page selections are:
    Configuration Description
    All events on/off
    Click to toggle to one of these states:
    • All events off
    • Partial
    • All events on
    Event Name Events are listed.
    Event On/Off

    Select it to turn events on. Deselect it to turn events off.

    If you have multiple events and you deselect one, the main All events on/off toggle changes to the Partial state.
  9. Click Save.
Enable events associated with Banner-owned resources from the Resources tab

Update the Ethos applications for Banner with any events that are associated with a resource that is owned by Banner.

Before you begin

  • Upgrade to the latest Banner version.
  • The event-configurations API must be installed on the Banner environment for these features to be available. See event-configurations.
  • To install an API in Banner, see Install Banner Ethos API.
  • Also see Set up the Banner Ethos APIs and supporting Banner software.

About this task

When you originally created the Ethos applications for Banner, you added the resources that Banner owns. A new version of the Banner might include events that are associated with the resources owned by Banner. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos applications for Banner with any events to Banner owned resources.

Perform this procedure for each Ethos application that you created for Banner Ethos APIs.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Resources.
  3. On the Resources page, locate the resource in the Resource column for which you want to enable events.
    If necessary, enter the resource name in the Search Resources field to locate it.
  4. On the resource that has the ability to configure events, click More and select Configure Events.
    The Events page displays for the selected resource.
  5. Optional: The Configure Events option displays only if the default resource owner has the ability to set up events.

    If the Configure Events option does not display in the menu, the event-configurations API is probably not in the Banner environment for that resource.

    Click the edit button in the Resource Owner column for the resource, select the correct environment, and click Confirm.

  6. Your Events page selections are:
    Configuration Description
    All events on/off
    Click this option to toggle to one of these states:
    • All events off
    • Partial
    • All events on
    Event Name Events are listed.
    Event On/Off

    Select it to turn events on. Clear it to turn events off.

    If you have multiple events and you deselect one, the main All events on/off toggle changes to the Partial state.
  7. Click Save.
Configure ISO Codes for Banner

If a Banner application owns the ISO code configuration APIs, you can configure the ISO codes for that application.

Before you begin

The minimum API release to use these features is Banner Ethos API 9.16 and Colleague Ethos API 1.24.

About this task

The Owned Resources page of the application contains a link to the API Configuration ISO Code Settings page if there are ISO code resources such as countries or currencies.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. Click View Applications.
  3. Click the authoritative source application.
    For Banner, you created an application in Ethos Integration for the Banner Integration API. Select the Banner Integration API application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
  5. Click Add Resources > Add Ellucian Ethos Resource(s) to add the following resources to be owned by Banner.
    • countries
    • country-iso-codes
    • currencies
    • currency-iso-codes
    • languages
    • language-iso-codes
    • regions
    • region-iso-codes
    • subregions
    • subregion-iso-codes
  6. Go back to the Applications landing page. On the application row, click the More icon, and then click API Configuration.
    The API Configuration ISO Codes page displays. You can configure ISO codes for Country, Currency, Language, Region, and Subregion.
  7. Click Edit to change the mapping selections.
    Note: You have the option to view recommendations for ISO codes and update the configuration based on recommended values. A recommended value displays in the Recommendations column if there is an exact match.
  8. Optional: Click Credentials for Configuration to specify if you want to enter new credentials or to use the credentials provided for auto-configure resources.
  9. Optional: Click Recommendations.
    The Recommendations column populates with suggested ISO codes.
  10. Click the selections you want and click Apply, or click Apply All to apply all recommendations.
    Note: If no recommendations are available, a message states there are no recommendations.
  11. Optional: Deselect Recommendations and click Filter in the ISO Code column to filter by Country in the Regions tab and to filter by Region in the Subregions tab.
  12. Optional: Click Export to generate an Excel spreadsheet that contains the ISO codes for all ISO code tabs on the user interface.
Set up other applications to access Banner resources (non-MEP)

Other applications can access Banner resources through Ethos Integration by making proxy API requests or GraphQL requests, or by subscribing to data changes.

Note: Currently, Banner Business Process APIs do not support GraphQL requests or Ethos Change Notifications.
