Setting up other applications is not part of initial setup of Banner with Ethos Integration. Instead, you will perform these procedures when you set up the other application in Ethos Integration.

For some Ellucian applications, there are specific procedures for setup in Ethos Integration. For other applications or your own custom application, use the general procedures in Set up applications in Ethos Integration (single owner).

Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (MEP - single tenant)

For a Banner Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation, create the Ethos applications and add the resources for which Banner is authoritative, and set up other applications to access those resources.

For a Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation of Banner, the recommended configuration in Ethos involves set up steps across multiple tenants. See Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (MEP - multiple tenants).

For a single-entity (non-MEP) implementation of Banner, see Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (non-MEP).

Install the database function for identification of shared resources (MEP - single tenant)

Install a database function in your Banner database that identifies which Ethos resources correspond to your segregated (MEP-enabled) Banner tables, and which resources correspond to your shared Banner tables.

About this task

The Ellucian Message Adapter calls this database function during processing, and you will run a script that calls this database function when you set up the shared resources Ethos applications.

Procedure

Follow the instructions in Setting up shared and MEPed resources with EMA 4.0 in a MEPed environment in the Ellucian Customer Center to install the database function in the Banner database.
Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (MEP - single tenant)

The Ethos Integration application records contain basic information about Banner, including the location of the Banner Student and Integration APIs, the resources for which Banner is responsible, and the API key.

About this task

Perform this procedure multiple times to create the following applications:
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Student API.
  • One application for shared resources for the Student API.
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Integration API.
  • One application for shared resources for the Integration API.
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Business Process API.
For example, if your MEP implementation includes two MEP instances, for the Main Campus and North Campus, you would create the following applications:
  • Banner Student Main
  • Banner Student North
  • Banner Student Shared
  • Banner Integration Main
  • Banner Integration North
  • Banner Integration Shared
  • Banner Business Process Main
  • Banner Business Process North

The Application Setup Wizard automatically adds ownership of Ethos resources to the application. It will get the list of resources to add by calling the /resources endpoint of the API.

Be sure to create the Student API, Integration API, and Business Process API applications for your primary MEP instance (for example, main campus) first, and then create the applications for the other MEP instances. This will save you work later when you set up other applications to make proxy API requests for resources owned by Banner. When a resource is owned by multiple Ethos Integration applications, the application that owned it first becomes the initial default owner. You can change the default owner later. Any proxy API request for a resource will go to the default owner unless you create a resource request to redirect the request to a different owner. By creating the applications for your primary MEP instance first, you will limit the need to specify default owners and create resource requests, assuming that most of the proxy API requests should go to that primary instance.

The Application Setup Wizard automatically adds ownership of Ethos resources to the application. After you create all of the applications, each Ethos application of the same API type will own the same Ethos resources. For example, all of the Student API applications (Banner Student Main, Banner Student North, and Banner Student Shared) will own the section-registrations resource. In a later procedure, you will remove owned resources from the shared resources applications so that they own only the resources that are shared across your MEP installation.

If you are using Cross-Registration, see Create Ethos applications for other applications that access Banner (MEP - multiple tenants).

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, in the Create New App area, select From Catalog.
    The Browse Catalog page displays.
  4. On the Browse Catalog page, search for and select the Ellucian Banner application and select Create App.
    The catalog populates the resources owned by Banner.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.

    Examples: Banner Student Main, Banner Integration North, or Banner Business Process North
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. On the Select Catalog Application page of the wizard, enter the following information and click Next:
    Field Entry
    Designated Owner of Shared Data If this is one of the applications for shared resources, select this check box.
    Base URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/<vpdi>/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Student API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/<vpdi>/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Integration API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminBPAPI/api/<vpdi>, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Business Process API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    Note: If this is one of the applications for shared resources, you still must enter a valid VPDI code, even though the shared application is not associated with a particular MEP instance. You can enter the VPDI code from any MEP instance.
    Base QAPI URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/<vpdi>/qapi

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/<vpdi>/qapi

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminAPI/<vpdi>/qapi

    Username/Password Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API. See Define user privileges for API access.
    Note: For applications that are specific to a MEP instance, the wizard creates a tag for that application. The value of the tag is your entry for <vpdi>. No tag is created for a shared application. After creating the application, you can see the tag on the Tags tab on the Application Overview page. Other Ellucian solutions, including Data Access, use this tag to access the appropriate MEP instance during processing.
  7. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    Banner does not subscribe to changes published by other Ethos applications.
  8. Optional: On the Finish page of the wizard, to unrestrict the restricted API key you created:
    1. Click Edit your new API key to allow IP access.
      The Edit API Key page displays. By default, Set API key to have IP address restrictions is selected.
    2. To add an IP address that is not restricted, enter the CIDR block for the Source IP Address.
    3. To add multiple IP addresses, enter a comma-separated list of IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks that are allowed to use the API key.
      When you make an API key available for use for one or multiple Ellucian products, use the following IP addresses:
         
      Ellucian Experience Experience domains and IP addresses
      Intelligent Learning Platform ILP domains and IP addresses
      Ellucian Workflow Ellucian Workflow NAT gateway IP addresses
      Ethos Data Connect Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses
    4. Click Save.
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure application-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the application now and configure settings later.
Limit the resources owned by the shared resources applications (MEP - single tenant)

You created two Ethos applications for shared resources: one for the Student API and one for the Integration API. Those applications must own only the resources that are shared across your MEP implementation.

About this task

When your institution set up Banner MEP, you identified the data that should be segregated (unique to each MEP instance). The Banner tables that contain segregated data were MEP-enabled by assigning a VPDI code to the table in the Banner database. For example, your institution might have decided that the information about people in the SPRIDEN table should be shared across all MEP instances, so the SPRIDEN table would not have been MEP-enabled. However, because buildings data is unique to each MEP instance, the STVBLDG table might have been MEP-enabled.

When you created the two Ethos applications for shared resources, the Application Setup Wizard automatically added ownership of all resources that Banner typically owns for that API type (Student or Integration API). Using the procedure below, you will remove all segregated resources (that is, resources that correspond to your MEP-enabled Banner tables) from those applications.

Note: You do not need to modify the Ethos applications that you created for each MEP instance. Those applications will own both the shared and segregated resources, but Ethos Integration knows that shared resources should be published through the shared resources applications.

Procedure

  1. Follow the instructions in Article 000045063 in the Ellucian Customer Center to run a script that identifies shared resources.
    The output of the script is a list of which Ethos resources correspond to your segregated (MEP-enabled) Banner tables, and which resources correspond to your shared Banner tables.
  2. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  3. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  4. On the Applications page, locate the tile for the application that you created for Student API shared resources, and click Edit .
  5. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  6. On the Owned Resources page, delete each of the MEPed resources for the Student API, based on the script that you ran in Step 1.
    The MEPed resources should not be owned by the shared resources application.
  7. Repeat Step 3 through Step 6 for the Integration API.
Update Banner's owned resources after an Ethos API upgrade (MEP - single tenant)

Update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to Banner's owned resources resulting from a new version of the Banner Ethos APIs.

About this task

When you originally created the applications for Banner, you added the resources that Banner owns. A new version of the Banner Ethos APIs can include changes to the resources owned by Banner. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to the resources owned by Banner.

Perform this procedure for each Ethos application that you created for Banner Ethos APIs.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the Banner application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. Click Auto-Configure Resources.
  6. In the Request Resources from Application window, enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API.
  7. Click Next.
    The list of resources owned by Banner is automatically updated to reflect changes in the new version of the APIs.
  8. Click Close.
Set up other applications to access Banner resources (MEP - single tenant)

Other applications can access Banner resources through Ethos Integration by making proxy API requests or GraphQL requests, or by subscribing to data changes.

Note: Currently, Banner Business Process APIs do not support GraphQL requests or Ethos Change Notifications.

Setting up other applications is not part of initial setup of Banner with Ethos Integration. Instead, you will perform these procedures when you set up the other application in Ethos Integration.

Note: These are general procedures for setting up applications in Ethos Integration for Banner MEP. For some Ellucian applications, there are product-specific procedures that you should use instead of these general procedures.
Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - single tenant)

If this application will make proxy API requests to Banner, create a Banner user with the required permissions.

In Banner, create a user with the required permissions to access the data models needed by the requesting software application. For the procedure for creating that user, see the Banner Ethos APIs section of the Ellucian API Documentation. In the information for Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs, go to the appropriate domain (such as Foundation APIs or Student APIs) for the data model, and then go to the Security Overview section to see the required permissions.

You will enter the user credentials when you set up proxy API requests in the requesting application, which you can do either in the Add Application wizard or later by editing the application.

Create Ethos applications for other applications that access Banner (MEP - single tenant)

In Ethos Integration, create Ethos applications for the other application that needs to access Banner MEP.

Before you begin

The Add Application wizard will prompt you for information about the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for this application. Before running the wizard, determine the needs of this application:
  • If this application needs to make proxy API requests to Banner, create a Banner user for authentication of those requests. See Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - single tenant).
  • If this application needs to make GraphQL requests to Data Access, determine the resources that this application needs to access using those requests.
  • If this application needs to subscribe to data changes published by Banner, determine the resources to which this application needs to subscribe.

About this task

Typically, you create one Ethos application for each Banner MEP instance, as described in Example: Banner MEP and Campus Card System. Using the Campus Card example, if your MEP implementation includes two MEP instances, for the Main Campus and North Campus, you would create the following Ethos applications:
  • Campus Card System Main
  • Campus Card System North
This procedure uses the Add Application wizard to manually create an Ethos application and set up the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for the application. Other options for performing these functions are:
  • For some Ellucian applications, including Banner and Colleague, you can select the application from a catalog, which automatically configures the appropriate owned resources and subscriptions. See the product-specific documentation for setting up each Ellucian application in Ethos Integration to determine whether the catalog method is supported and to see the procedure.
  • You can set up or modify proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions by editing the application after you create it.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, click Add Application.
  4. In the Add Application dialog box, do the following:
    1. If this application will make proxy API requests to retrieve data from another application, select Configure REST API proxy.
    2. If this application will make GraphQL requests to retrieve data from Data Access, select Configure GraphQL resources.
    3. Click Continue.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. If you selected Configure REST API proxy in the first step of the wizard, set up proxy API requests on the Add Source Applications page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Source Application to open the Add Source Application dialog box.
    2. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Student API for the appropriate MEP instance.
    3. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    4. In the Select a resource field, select any Ethos resource to which that user account has permissions in Banner. For example, persons.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    5. Click Add.
    6. Repeat Steps 6.a through 6.e for the Banner Integration API.
    7. Click Next.
  7. If you selected Configure GraphQL resources in the first step of the wizard, set up GraphQL requests on the Add Resources page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Resources.
    2. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
      If you entered credentials for source applications (Step 6), only the resources owned by those source applications are available for selection. If not, all resources owned by any application in this environment are available.
    3. Click Add.
    4. If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data through GraphQL requests, and then click Add.
      If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for GraphQL requests have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
    5. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, continue with the next step. Otherwise, click Next and skip to Step 8.
      For example, you might have loaded persons data into Data Access from Banner or Colleague. You want this application to be able to access most persons information, but not the dateOfBirth property. You would add the persons resource and then use the steps below to hide the dateOfBirth property.
      Note: For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example attribute filters for GraphQL resources.
    6. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to hide, and then click Show more .
    7. In the Attribute Filters area, click the Add icon.
    8. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to hide.
      For example, to hide the date of birth property in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

    9. If you want the property to be hidden from this application only under certain conditions, click Add Criteria and then enter the criteria:
      Field Entry
      Property Path Enter the path to the data model property to be used in the criterion. This property must be in the same resource as the property that you are hiding.
      Operator Select equals or not equals
      Criteria Enter the value of this property that will determine whether the criterion is met.
    10. Click Next.
  8. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    This version of the select release software does not currently support adding subscriptions from within the wizard in a Banner MEP implementation. If this application subscribes to Banner changes, you can add them later using the procedure in Set up an application to subscribe to changes published by Banner (MEP - single tenant).
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure app-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the app now and configure settings later.
Set up an application to subscribe to changes published by Banner (MEP - single tenant)

Set up an application to access data from Banner MEP by subscribing to published change notifications.

About this task

Note the following about setting up subscriptions:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add subscriptions to an existing Ethos application. You can also add subscriptions when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required subscriptions when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to these procedures performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the subscribing software application to retrieve change notifications from Ethos Integration. See Retrieve messages.

Perform the procedure below for each Ethos application that you created. In the example used earlier, you would perform this procedure twice, one time for the Campus Card System Main application and one time for the Campus Card System North application.

In a Banner MEP implementation, resources are owned by multiple Ethos applications. As you add each subscription, you will need to select the appropriate instance of each owned resource. The table below shows an example.

Table 1. Example: Subscribing to changes published by Banner MEP
This Ethos application... ...subscribes to change notifications published by these Ethos applications
Campus Card System Main

Banner Student Main

Banner Student Shared

Banner Integration Main

Banner Integration Shared
Campus Card System North

Banner Student North

Banner Student Shared

Banner Integration North

Banner Integration Shared

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate the tile for the subscribing Ethos application and then click Edit .
    Using the earlier example, you could click the tile for the Campus Card System Main application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Resource Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Subscriptions.
  6. In the Add Subscriptions dialog box, do the following for each resource to which your application needs to subscribe:
    1. Select the check box next to the resource.
      Ethos Integration displays all of the owners of that resource.
    2. Select the instance of the resource (that is, select the owning application) to which you want to subscribe.
      If one of the owners is a shared resources application, select that application. For example, if the list of owners is as shown below, you would select Banner Student Shared.
      • Banner Student Main
      • Banner Student North
      • Banner Student Shared
      If none of the owners is a shared resources application, select the owner for the appropriate MEP instance. For example, if you are setting up the Campus Card System Main application, and the list of owners is as shown below, you would select Banner Student Main.
      • Banner Student Main
      • Banner Student North
  7. After you select all the desired subscriptions, click Add.
  8. Repeat Step 3 through Step 7 for each Ethos application that you created for the subscribing application.
    Using the earlier example, you would perform these steps for Campus Card System Main and then for Campus Card System North.
Add credentials for proxy API requests to Banner (MEP - single tenant)

In the Ethos applications that you created for the requesting application, add the Banner credentials that allow that application to access Banner data.

Before you begin

Before performing this procedure, create a Banner user with the required permissions to access the data models needed by the requesting software application. See Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - single tenant).

About this task

Perform the procedure below for each Ethos application that you created for the requesting application. In the example used earlier, you would perform this procedure twice, one time for the Campus Card System Main application and one time for the Campus Card System North application.

Each requesting application makes proxy API requests to its appropriate MEP instance through both the Student API and the Integration API. The table below shows an example. For each requesting application, you will enter credentials for both the Student API and the Integration API.

Table 1. Example: Credentials for proxy API requests to Banner MEP
In this Ethos application... ...you enter credentials for these Ethos applications
Campus Card System Main Banner Student Main

Banner Integration Main
Campus Card System North Banner Student North

Banner Integration North

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate the tile for the requesting Ethos application and then click Edit .
    Using the earlier example, you could click the tile for the Campus Card System Main application.
  4. On the page, click the Credentials tab.
  5. Click Add Credentials.
  6. In the Add Credentials dialog box, do the following:
    1. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Student API for the appropriate MEP instance.
      Using the earlier example, you would select the Banner Student Main application.
    2. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    3. In the Select a resource field, select any resource for which you granted that user account permissions in Banner. For example, sections.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner Student Main. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    4. Click Add Credentials.
  7. Back on the Application Overview page, click Add Credentials again.
  8. In the Add Credentials dialog box, do the following:
    1. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Integration API for the appropriate MEP instance.
      Using the earlier example, you would select the Banner Integration Main application.
    2. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    3. Select any resource for which you granted that user account permissions in Banner. For example, persons.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner Integration Main.
    4. Click Add Credentials.
  9. Repeat Step 3 through Step 8 for each Ethos application that you created for the requesting application.
    Using the earlier example, you would perform these steps for Campus Card System Main and then for Campus Card System North.
Add GraphQL resources to an application (MEP - single tenant)

Set up an application to make GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access in a Banner MEP environment.

About this task

Note the following about setting up GraphQL requests:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add GraphQL resources to an existing Ethos application. You can also add GraphQL resources when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required resources when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to this procedure performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the requesting application to make a GraphQL request to Ethos Integration. See Make GraphQL requests to Data Access.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the GraphQL Resources tab.
  5. Click Add Resources.
  6. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
    If you entered credentials for source applications (typically the Banner Student and Integration APIs for this MEP instance), either in the Add Application wizard or on the Credentials tab, only the resources owned by those source applications are available for selection. If not, all resources owned by any application in this environment are available.
  7. Click Add.
    In this case, if you add a resource and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will not be available for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.
  8. If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data through GraphQL requests, and then click Add.
    If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for GraphQL requests have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
  9. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, perform the steps below to hide the properties.
    For example, you might have loaded persons data into Data Access from Banner or Colleague. You want this application to be able to access most persons information, but not the dateOfBirth property. You would add the persons resource and then use the steps below to hide the dateOfBirth property.
    Note: For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example attribute filters for GraphQL resources.
    1. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to hide, and then click Show more .
    2. In the Attribute Filters area, click the Add icon.
    3. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to hide.
      For example, to hide the date of birth property in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

    4. If you want the property to be hidden from this application only under certain conditions, click Add Criteria and then enter the criteria:
      Field Entry
      Property Path Enter the path to the data model property to be used in the criterion. This property must be in the same resource as the property that you are hiding.
      Operator Select equals or not equals
      Criteria Enter the value of this property that will determine whether the criterion is met.
    5. After defining all filters for this resource, click Save.
Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (MEP - multiple tenants)

For a Banner Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation, create the Ethos applications and add the resources for which Banner is authoritative, and set up other applications to access those resources.

For a single-entity (non-MEP) implementation of Banner, see Set up Banner in Ethos Integration (non-MEP).

For a Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation of Banner, the recommended configuration in Ethos involves set up steps across multiple tenants.

Note: This configuration option is required when using Cross Registration. See Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (MEP - multiple tenants).
Create the applications in Ethos Integration for Banner (MEP - multiple tenants)

The Ethos Integration application records contain basic information about Banner, including the location of the Banner Student APIs and Banner Integration APIsIntegration APIs, the resources for which Banner is responsible, and the API key.

About this task

Perform this procedure multiple times to create the following applications. Each time you perform this procedure, it will be in a different tenant.
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Student API.
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Integration API.
  • For each MEP instance, an application for the Business Process API.
For example, if your MEP implementation includes two MEP instances, for the Main Campus and North Campus, you would create the following applications in the Main Campus tenant and in the North Campus tenant:
  • Banner Student
  • Banner Integration
  • Banner Business Process

The Application Setup Wizard automatically adds ownership of Ethos resources to the application. It will get the list of resources to add by calling the /resources endpoint of the API.

The multiple tenant configuration option described below is the recommended setup for a Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementation of Banner.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, in the Create New App area, select From Catalog.
    The Browse Catalog page displays.
  4. On the Browse Catalog page, search for and select the Ellucian Banner application and then select Create App.
    The catalog populates the resources owned by Banner.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.

    Examples: Banner Student, Banner Integration, or Banner Business Process
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. On the Select Catalog Application page of the wizard, enter the following information and click Next:
    Field Entry
    Designated Owner of Shared Data This option is not used for a multiple tenant setup.
    Base URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/<vpdi>/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Student API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/<vpdi>/api, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Integration API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminBPAPI/api/<vpdi>, where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Business Process API, and <vpdi> is the VPDI code for this MEP instance.

    Base QAPI URI For the Banner Student API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/<vpdi>/qapi

    For the Banner Integration API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/<vpdi>/qapi

    For the Banner Business Process API application, enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminAPI/<vpdi>/qapi

    Username/Password Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API. See Define user privileges for API access.
    Note: For applications that are specific to a MEP instance, the wizard creates a tag for that application. The value of the tag is your entry for <vpdi>. After creating the application, you can see the tag on the Tags tab on the Application Overview page. Other Ellucian solutions, including Data Access, use this tag to access the appropriate MEP instance during processing.
  7. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    Banner does not subscribe to changes published by other Ethos applications.
  8. Optional: On the Finish page of the wizard, to unrestrict the restricted API key you created:
    1. Click Edit your new API key to allow IP access.
      The Edit API Key page displays. By default, Set API key to have IP address restrictions is selected.
    2. To add an IP address that is not restricted, enter the CIDR block for the Source IP Address.
    3. To add multiple IP addresses, enter a comma-separated list of IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks that are allowed to use the API key.
      When you make an API key available for use for one or multiple Ellucian products, use the following IP addresses:
         
      Ellucian Experience Experience domains and IP addresses
      Intelligent Learning Platform ILP domains and IP addresses
      Ellucian Workflow Ellucian Workflow NAT gateway IP addresses
      Ethos Data Connect Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses
    4. Click Save.
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure application-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the application now and configure settings later.
Update Banner's owned resources after an Ethos API upgrade (MEP - multiple tenants)

Update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to Banner's owned resources resulting from a new version of the Banner Ethos APIs.

About this task

When you originally created the applications for Banner, you added the resources that Banner owns. A new version of the Banner Ethos APIs can include changes to the resources owned by Banner. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos applications for Banner with any changes to the resources owned by Banner.

Perform this procedure for each Ethos application that you created for Banner Ethos APIs.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the Banner application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. Click Auto-Configure Resources.
  6. In the Request Resources from Application window, enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner API.
  7. Click Next.
    The list of resources owned by Banner is automatically updated to reflect changes in the new version of the APIs.
  8. Click Close.
Set up other applications to access Banner resources (MEP - multiple tenants)

Other applications can access Banner resources through Ethos Integration by making proxy API requests or GraphQL requests, or by subscribing to data changes.

Note: Currently, Banner Business Process APIs do not support GraphQL requests or Ethos Change Notifications.

Setting up other applications is not part of initial setup of Banner with Ethos Integration. Instead, you will perform these procedures when you set up the other application in Ethos Integration.

Note: These are general procedures for setting up applications in Ethos Integration for Banner MEP. For some Ellucian applications, there are product-specific procedures that you should use instead of these general procedures.
Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - multiple tenants)

If this application will make proxy API requests to Banner, create a Banner user with the required permissions.

In Banner, create a user with the required permissions to access the data models needed by the requesting software application. For the procedure for creating that user, see the Banner Ethos APIs section of the Ellucian API Documentation. In the information for Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs, go to the appropriate domain (such as Foundation APIs or Student APIs) for the data model, and then go to the Security Overview section to see the required permissions.

You will enter the user credentials when you set up proxy API requests in the requesting application, which you can do either in the Add Application wizard or later by editing the application.

Create Ethos applications for other applications that access Banner (MEP - multiple tenants)

In Ethos Integration, create Ethos applications for the other application that needs to access Banner MEP.

Before you begin

The Add Application wizard will prompt you for information about the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for this application. Before running the wizard, determine the needs of this application:
  • If this application needs to make proxy API requests to Banner, create a Banner user for authentication of those requests. See Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - multiple tenants).
  • If this application needs to make GraphQL requests to Data Access, determine the resources that this application needs to access using those requests.
  • If this application needs to subscribe to data changes published by Banner, determine the resources to which this application needs to subscribe.

About this task

You would create an application, such as a Campus Card System, in each tenant for getting information from the various Banner MEP applications.

This procedure uses the Add Application wizard to manually create an Ethos application and set up the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for the application. Other options for performing these functions are:
  • For some Ellucian applications, including Banner and Colleague, you can select the application from a catalog, which automatically configures the appropriate owned resources and subscriptions. See the product-specific documentation for setting up each Ellucian application in Ethos Integration to determine whether the catalog method is supported and to see the procedure.
  • You can set up or modify proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions by editing the application after you create it.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, click Add Application.
  4. In the Add Application dialog box, do the following:
    1. If this application will make proxy API requests to retrieve data from another application, select Configure REST API proxy.
    2. If this application will make GraphQL requests to retrieve data from Data Access, select Configure GraphQL resources.
    3. Click Continue.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. If you selected Configure REST API proxy in the first step of the wizard, set up proxy API requests on the Add Source Applications page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Source Application to open the Add Source Application dialog box.
    2. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Student API.
    3. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    4. In the Select a resource field, select any Ethos resource to which that user account has permissions in Banner. For example, sections.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    5. Click Add.
    6. Repeat Steps 6.a through 6.e for the Banner Integration API.
    7. Click Next.
  7. If you selected Configure GraphQL resources in the first step of the wizard, set up GraphQL requests on the Add Resources page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Resources.
    2. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
      If you entered credentials for source applications (Step 6), only the resources owned by those source applications are available for selection. If not, all resources owned by any application in this environment are available.
    3. Click Add.
    4. If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data through GraphQL requests, and then click Add.
      If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for GraphQL requests have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
    5. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, continue with the next step. Otherwise, click Next and skip to Step 8.
      For example, you might have loaded persons data into Data Access from Banner or Colleague. You want this application to be able to access most persons information, but not the dateOfBirth property. You would add the persons resource and then use the steps below to hide the dateOfBirth property.
      Note: For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example attribute filters for GraphQL resources.
    6. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to hide, and then click Show more .
    7. In the Attribute Filters area, click the Add icon.
    8. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to hide.
      For example, to hide the date of birth property in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

    9. If you want the property to be hidden from this application only under certain conditions, click Add Criteria and then enter the criteria:
      Field Entry
      Property Path Enter the path to the data model property to be used in the criterion. This property must be in the same resource as the property that you are hiding.
      Operator Select equals or not equals
      Criteria Enter the value of this property that will determine whether the criterion is met.
    10. Click Next.
  8. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    This version of the select release software does not currently support adding subscriptions from within the wizard in a Banner MEP implementation. If this application subscribes to Banner changes, you can add them later using the procedure in Set up an application to subscribe to changes published by Banner (MEP - multiple tenants).
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure app-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the app now and configure settings later.
Set up an application to subscribe to changes published by Banner (MEP - multiple tenants)

Set up an application to access data from Banner MEP by subscribing to published change notifications.

About this task

Note the following about setting up subscriptions:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add subscriptions to an existing Ethos application. You can also add subscriptions when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required subscriptions when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to these procedures performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the subscribing software application to retrieve change notifications from Ethos Integration. See Retrieve messages.

Perform the procedure below in each MEP campus tenant. In the example used earlier, you would perform this procedure twice, creating a Campus Card System application in the Main Campus tenant and in the North Campus tenant.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate the tile for the subscribing Ethos application and then click Edit .
    Using the earlier example, you could click the tile for the Campus Card System application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Resource Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Subscriptions.
  6. In the Add Subscriptions dialog box, do the following for each resource to which your application needs to subscribe:
    1. Select the check box next to the resource.
      Ethos Integration displays all of the owners of that resource.
    2. If needed, select the instance of the resource (that is, select the owning application) to which you want to subscribe.
  7. After you select all the desired subscriptions, click Add.
  8. Repeat Step 3 through Step 7 for each Ethos application that you created for the subscribing application.
    Using the earlier example, you would perform these steps for the Campus Card System application in the Main Campus tenant and the North Campus tenant.
Add credentials for proxy API requests to Banner (MEP - multiple tenants)

In the Ethos applications that you created for the requesting application, add the Banner credentials that allow that application to access Banner data.

Before you begin

Before performing this procedure, create a Banner user with the required permissions to access the data models needed by the requesting software application. See Create a Banner user for proxy API requests (MEP - multiple tenants).

About this task

Perform the procedure below in each MEP campus tenant. In the example used earlier, you would perform this procedure twice, creating a Campus Card System application in the Main Campus tenant and in the North Campus tenant.

Table 1. Example: Credentials for proxy API requests to Banner MEP
In this Ethos application... ...you would enter credentials for these Ethos applications

Campus Card System Main

Campus Card System North

 Banner Student

Banner Integration

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate the tile for the requesting Ethos application and then click Edit .
    Using the earlier example, you could click the tile for the Campus Card System Main application.
  4. On the page, click the Credentials tab.
  5. Click Add Credentials.
  6. In the Add Credentials dialog box, do the following:
    1. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Student API.
    2. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    3. Select any resource for which you granted that user account permissions in Banner. For example, sections.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner Student. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    4. Click Add Credentials.
  7. Back on the Application Overview page, click Add Credentials again.
  8. In the Add Credentials dialog box, do the following:
    1. In the Source application field, select the application for the Banner Integration API.
    2. Enter the username and password for the user that you created in Banner.
    3. In the Select a resource field, select any resource for which you granted that user account permissions in Banner. For example, persons.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner Integration. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    4. Click Add Credentials.
  9. Repeat Step 3 through Step 8 for each Ethos application that you created for the requesting application.
    Using the earlier example, you would perform these steps for the Campus Card System application in the Main Campus tenant and in the North Campus tenant.

Set up Banner with Data Access

If your integration will use GraphQL requests to read Banner data stored in Ellucian Ethos Data Access, you need to set up the loading of Banner data into Data Access.

Only the data from Banner Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs are available for loading into Data Access. Currently, Data Access does not load with Business Process APIs.

See The data load process and Configure Data Access.

Specify EMS settings in Banner

Define settings that the Ellucian Message Adapter uses to link the Ellucian Messaging Service with Banner.

About this task

To enter these settings, you will need the values you entered when setting up the RabbitMQ server.

Procedure

  1. Log in to Banner and access the Integration Configuration Settings (GORICCR) page to configure the settings.
  2. Click the Configuration tab.
  3. On the Configuration page, click the EMS Settings tab.
  4. In the left pane, click ethos-integration.
  5. Enter the AMQP settings:
    Name Ethos Value Example
    EMS AMQP autorecover Specify whether the RabbitMQ connection failures should auto-recover (Y or N).
    Note: For initial setup, you can accept the default.
    		  
    EMS AMQP heartbeat Enter the frequency of any keep-alive signal sent to RabbitMQ (seconds).
    Note: For initial setup, you can accept the default.
    		 30
    EMS AMQP host Enter the RabbitMQ server host. rabbitmq.​mycollege.​edu
    EMS AMQP port Enter the RabbitMQ server port 5671 for secure, 5672 for non-secure
    EMS AMQP secure Enter Y if you configured RabbitMQ for SSL. Enter N if you did not configure RabbitMQ for SSL.  
    EMS AMQP timeout Enter the RabbitMQ connection timeout (seconds).
    Note: For initial setup, you can accept the default.
    		 900
    EMS AMQP virtualhost Enter the RabbitMQ virtual host that you specified during Ellucian Messaging Service installation. bep_events_host
  6. Enter the Ethos Integration settings:
    Note: If you are in a region other than the U.S., substitute your region-specific domain in place of integrate.elluciancloud.com in the examples. See Ethos Integration domains.
    Note: If you are whitelisting outbound traffic, configure EMA to use the static hostnames from IPs to whitelist.
    Setting Entry
    EMS Ethos Integration MEP API keys You can ignore this field. It is not used with EMA 2.4.1 and later.
    EMS Ethos Integration MEP enabled Enter Y if this is a MEP-enabled environment.
    EMS Ethos Integration application API key You can ignore this field. It is not used with EMA 2.4.1 and later.
    EMS Ethos Integration error URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/​errors

    or

    https://errors-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/errors
    EMS Ethos Integration mediatype Enter application/vnd.hedtech.change-notifications.v2+json
    EMS Ethos Integration publish URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/​publish

    or

    https://messages-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/publish
    EMS Ethos Integration token URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/​auth

    or

    https://tokens-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/auth
    EMS Ethos Integration use Enter Y
  7. Enter the GUID lifespan setting:
    Setting Entry Example
    EMS GUID lifespan Enter the length of time a record update will block reverse updates (in seconds).
    Note: For initial setup, you can accept the default.
    		 30
  8. Specify names for the RabbitMQ topic exchange and queue for BEP:
    When you deploy the Ellucian Message Adapter and it starts for the first time, it will create this topic exchange and queue.
    Setting Entry Example
    EMS event ERP exchangename Enter the name of the topic exchange that you specified when you installed the Banner Event Publisher and configured BEP settings in the BannerEventPublisher_​configuration.​groovy file. bep_events_topic
    EMS event ERP queuename Specify a name for the RabbitMQ queue for the Ellucian Message Adapter.

    Record this value in the Banner/Ethos Integration worksheet.

    		 ema_queue
  9. Specify the logging level:
    Setting Entry Example
    EMS log level Specify the maximum detail level of any logging. The available logging levels are:
    • FATAL
    • ERROR
    • WARN
    • INFO
    • DEBUG
    • TRACE
    		 Suggested levels:
    • DEBUG for initial setup and troubleshooting
    • ERROR during normal operation
  10. If this is an update to the configuration for an existing installation, restart the Ellucian Message Adapter so that the changes take effect.

Create and Authorize a Banner User to Enable Proxy API calls for Ethos Integration

Create administrative Oracle users in Banner and assign the appropriate API permissions, to allow those users to make proxy API calls to Ethos integration.

There are some minor differences in setting up a Banner user for the Banner Business Process APIs compared to the Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs.

The below subsections describe steps for creating a new Banner user and assigning the user permissions for the Ethos APIs. The item of significance is the content regarding the specific classes used for the Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs. All the class names with API are specific to the Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs.

Use the same procedures to set up a user for the Administrative page while setting up a Banner user for calling the Business Process APIs. Business Process APIs use the same security classes referred to on the Administrative page.

For more information, see Security.

Create a Banner user

Procedure

  1. Work with your database administrator for URL access to the Banner Access Management application, which is where the Banner Security pages are located.
    Note: For detailed information about administering Banner Security, see Security.
  2. Log in to Banner Access Management.
  3. Navigate to the Oracle/Banner Security Maintenance (GSASECR) page.
  4. On the Users tab, enter a User ID. For example, API_USER.
  5. Click Create.
  6. Enter a password in the Password and Verify Password fields.
  7. In the Temporary Tablespace field, select a value from the List of Values.
  8. In the Default Tablespace field, select a value from the List of Values.
  9. In the Default Role field, enter USR_DEFAULT_CONNECT as the default role.
  10. In the Profile field, select a value from the List of Values.
  11. Select the Authorize BANPROXY check box.
  12. Select the Authorize BANJSPROXY check box.
  13. Click Save to create the new user ID.
  14. Optional: To enter information that applies to the institution, click Banner Rules. Enter any appropriate information and click Save.
  15. Optional: If Banner has been configured for MEP, the user must be authorized for any VPDI contexts that will be accessed from APIs. Navigate to the Oracle/Banner VPD Security Maintenance (GSAVPDI) form. To give a user access to the institution code other than the code that is set as the system default, click the User Assignment tab and assign the appropriate values.
Assign privileges to the Banner user

Assign the applicable Banner security objects to users who need access to a particular resource.

Before you begin

Refer to Security Objects and Classes under the Install section of the Banner Ethos API Administration documentation. Select a domain to see the list of resources and their associated security objects.

Procedure

  1. From the Users tab of the GSASECR page, select the User ID and click the Modify button to access the User/Class Privilege Maintenance page.
  2. Enter GUAGMNU in the Object Name field and click Save.
  3. To assign privileges to all objects within a user class:
    1. Make sure you are aware of all objects that a part of any classes assigned to the user.
    2. To review the list of objects that are part of a user class:
      1. Exit the Modify page of GSASECR.
      2. From the main page of GSASECR, click the Classes tab.
      3. Filter for records where Class Code Contains API.
      4. Select the Class Code in which you are interested, then click the Objects button to view the list of objects for this class.
      5. After you have reviewed all the classes in which you are interested, exit this page. Click the Users tab and click the Modify button to return to the User/Class Privilege Maintenancepage.
    3. Click the User Classes button.
    4. Filter for records where Class Code Contains API.
    5. Select one or more Class Code. Note that when you click on a Class Code to select it, the value of User In Class toggles between YES and NULL.
    6. Click Save.
  4. To assign privileges individual objects within a user class:
    1. Insert a record on the User/Class Privilege page.
    2. Select the Object Name from the List of Values that represent the resource for which you want to grant access.

Configure and deploy the Ellucian Message Adapter with Banner

The Ellucian Message Adapter (EMA) publishes data changes from Banner to Ellucian Ethos Integration. Perform these procedures to configure the Ellucian Message Adapter and then deploy it to a Tomcat web server.

WebLogic is no longer supported as a web server.

EMA Java requirements:

EMA version Minimum Java version, compatible with version
5.0 11
5.1 and 5.2 Minimum 8, compatible with 11
5.3 Minimum 17
5.3.1 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
5.4.0 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
5.4.1 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
5.4.2 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
5.5.0 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
6.0.0 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
6.0.1 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
6.0.2 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
Tomcat requirements:
  • EMA 5.x requires Tomcat 9
  • EMA 6.x requires Tomcat 10
Define the EMA_CONFIG encryption key

The Ellucian Message Adapter uses the EMA_CONFIG encryption key to encrypt and decrypt sensitive information stored in the emsConfig.xml file.

Use the appropriate procedure for your web server to define the encryption key.

(Tomcat) Create the EMA_CONFIG environment variable

Perform this procedure if you are using the Tomcat web server.

About this task

If you previously created the EMA_CONFIG environment variable for an earlier version of the Ellucian Message Adapter, you can skip this procedure.

Procedure

  1. Create a user or system environment variable.
    If you create a user environment variable, it must be for the user that is running your web server.
    1. For the variable name, enter EMA_CONFIG
    2. For the variable value, enter any text string.
      This text string is the encryption key.
  2. Stop and restart the Tomcat web server.
Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter

Enter values in the configuration file that the Ellucian Message Adapter uses to communicate with the Ethos APIs and other Ellucian Ethos Integration components.

You will download the EMA zip file to a Windows or Linux server. The zip file includes a WAR file which contains the emsConfig.xml configuration file where you will enter the settings.

Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter on Windows with Banner

If you are installing the Ellucian Message Adapter zip file on a Windows server, perform this procedure to enter the configuration settings.

Before you begin

Before installing the Ellucian Message Adapter, determine the appropriate version for your implementation. See Identify Ethos Integration component versions for Banner.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Message Adapter ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads page.

    The ZIP file is named EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip where x.x.x is the version number.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as C:\ellucian\EMA.
  3. Unzip the EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip file.
    The ZIP file contains:
    • Ellucian Messaging Adapter WAR file.
    • emsConfig.template xml configuration file.
    • ConfigureEMS.bat batch file for Windows.
    • ConfigureEMS.sh shell script for Linux.
  4. Double click ConfigureEMS.bat to configure the Ellucian Message Adapter WAR file.
    CAUTION:
    Do not right-click and select Run as administrator.
  5. If prompted, enter the directory path where JAVA is installed.
    A Notepad window opens and displays the emsConfig.xml file.
  6. Enter the configuration settings.
    For guidance, see the configuration settings topic for your scenario:
    • EMA configuration settings for Banner (MEP - single tenant)
    • EMA configuration settings for Colleague
    Note: If this is an upgrade from an earlier version of the Ellucian Message Adapter, you can copy some of the values from the existing emsConfig.xml file contained in the Ellucian Message Adapter WAR file that is currently deployed.
  7. Save your changes to the configuration file, then close the text editor.
    The batch process updates the WAR file with the changes to the configuration file.

Results

The WAR file is now ready for deployment.
Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter on Linux with Banner

If you are installing the Ellucian Message Adapter zip file on a Linux server, perform this procedure to enter the configuration settings.

Before you begin

Before installing the Ellucian Message Adapter, determine the appropriate version for your implementation. See Identify Ethos Integration component versions for Banner.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Message Adapter ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads page.

    The ZIP file is named EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip where x.x.x is the version number.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ema.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command, replacing x.x.x with your version number. For example, 5.0.0.
    unzip EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip
  4. Change to the subdirectory that contains the unzipped files (replace x.x.x with your version number):
    cd EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x
    The ZIP file contains:
    • Ellucian Messaging Adapter WAR file.
    • emsConfig.template xml configuration file.
    • ConfigureEMS.bat batch file for Windows.
    • ConfigureEMS.sh shell script for Linux.
  5. To set permissions so that you can execute the shell script, enter the following command:
    chmod 700 ConfigureEMS.sh
  6. Enter the following command to extract the contents of the WAR file and open the configuration file in the vi editor.
    ./ConfigureEMS.sh
  7. Enter the configuration settings.
    For guidance, see the configuration settings topic for your scenario:
    • EMA configuration settings for Banner (MEP - single tenant)
    • EMA configuration settings for Colleague
    Note: If this is an upgrade from an earlier version of the Ellucian Message Adapter, you can copy some of the values from the existing emsConfig.xml file contained in the Ellucian Message Adapter WAR file that is currently deployed.
  8. Save your changes to the configuration file, then exit the vi editor.
    The shell script updates the WAR file with the changes to the configuration file.

Results

The WAR file is now ready for deployment.
EMA configuration settings for Banner (non-MEP)

This topic describes the entries in the emsConfig.xml file for Ellucian Message Adapter with Banner.

Click Attachment on this page to download the Example_emsConfig_EMA... file for your EMA version and ERP (Banner or Colleague).

General settings

XML Attribute Description
clientErpType Enter Banner
configId Accept the default entry of ETHOS-INTEGRATION.
tenantalias Enter the alias for the Ethos tenant. You can find this on the Settings drop-down menu on the integration UI. This field allows additional safeguards to prevent you from entering the incorrect API when you configure EMA.
amqpUsername Enter the username and password of a RabbitMQ user who can access the virtual host that you created for Ellucian Ethos Integration.

You specified the virtual host name and an administrative username and password when you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service. You can use the username and password that you entered there. If you do not remember it, use the RabbitMQ Management Console to identify that user.
amqpPassword

Banner Student API settings

In the <bannerStudentConfig> section, enter the values for your Banner Student API.

Enter the Banner Student API URL and user credentials:

XML Attribute Description
baseUrl Enter the base URL of the Banner Student API website, in the following form:

https://<hostname>:<port>/StudentApi/api

where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Student API.
username Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner Student API.

For a Banner MEP installation with EMA 4.0 or later, this must be the same user that you set up with permissions to access the database function that identifies shared and Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) resources.
password

In the <apiKeys> section, for a single-instance (non-MEP) implementation, enter the values in the table below.

XML Attribute Description
hubApiKey Enter the Ethos Integration API key for the Banner Student API application. To get the API key, edit the application record in Ethos Integration, go to API Keys, and copy the key.
vpdiCode Leave this setting blank.

Banner Integration API settings

In the <bannerIntegrationConfig> section, enter the values for your Banner Integration API.

Enter the Banner Integration API URL and user credentials:

XML Attribute Description
baseUrl Enter the base URL of the Banner Integration API website, in the following form:

https://<hostname>:<port>/IntegrationApi/api

where <hostname> is the name of your Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Integration API.
username Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the Banner Integration API.

For a Banner MEP installation with EMA 4.0 or later, this must be the same user that you set up with permissions to access the database function that identifies shared and Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) resources.
password

In the <apiKeys> section, for a single-instance (non-MEP) implementation, enter the values in the table below.

XML Attribute Description
hubApiKey Enter the Ethos Integration API Key for the Banner Integration API application. To get the API key, edit the application record in Ethos Integration, go to API Keys, and copy the key.
vpdiCode Leave this setting blank.

Custom API settings

EMA 4.1.0 and later supports publishing from one custom API in addition to the Banner Integration API and Banner Student API. If you have configured a custom API in Ethos Integration, enter the settings below in the <customApiConfig> section.

Enter the API URL and user credentials:

XML Attribute Description
baseUrl Enter the base URL of the custom API website.

Example: https://<hostname>:<port>/CustomApi/api
username Enter the username and password of a Banner account with access to the custom API.
password

In the <apiKeys> section, for a single-instance (non-MEP) implementation, enter the values in the table below.

XML Attribute Description
