Assign the organizational role to the warmup script user

Use the Assign Resource to Org Roles (AROR) form to assign the warmup script organizational role to the person created for the warmup script user.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the Assign Resource to Org Roles (AROR) form.
  2. At the Resource LookUp prompt, enter the ID of the person associated with a user and click OK.
  3. In the Organization Role Hierarchy Department field, enter the organizational role associated with the corresponding account, to which you added the correct permissions.

Additional user account setup

Specific APIs require additional user setup to access certain types of information.

For example, to access certain financial information a user needs access to general ledger accounts.

Setup for ledger-activities

To interact with Colleague General Ledger information, the user needs to have general ledger access.

For each user that requires access to general ledger information, you will need to complete the following:
  • Create a staff record for the user.
  • Create a GL role with access to all general ledger accounts.
  • Create a GL user definition and assign the GL access role.
Create a staff record for the user

Use the Staff and Volunteers (SVM) form to create a staff record for the user.

Before you begin

You must have already:
  • Created the user.
  • Created an operator record for the user.

About this task

For the user to have access to general ledger information, you need to create a staff record for the user if one does not already exist.
User Purpose Name Example
Proxy API user or EMA Admin user Colleague needs a staff record to provide staff access for the user. For the user, you could create a staff record with an ID similar to the ID that was set up for the user's person record.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the Staff and Volunteers (SVM) form.
  2. At the Staff LookUp prompt, select the person record for the user and enter Y to create a staff record.
  3. In the Staff Code field, enter a code for Ethos Integration.
    For example, ETHOS.
  4. Enter the operator ID for the user created on the Operator Definition (SOD) form.
  5. Enter a staff type.
  6. Save your changes on the SVM form.

What to do next

You can create a GL role with access to all general ledger accounts.
Create a GL role with access to all general ledger accounts

Use the GL Role Definition (GLRD) form to create a role in Colleague General Ledger that has access to all GL accounts.

About this task

If you already have a GL role with access to all GL accounts, you can skip this step.

For the user to have access to general ledger information, you need to create a GL role for the user if one does not already exist.

User Purpose Name Example
Proxy API user or EMA Admin user Colleague needs a GL role to grant the user access to all GL accounts. For a user, you could create a role with a name similar to ETHOS_ALL_ACCESS.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the GL Role Definition (GLRD) form.
  2. At the GL Role LookUp prompt, enter the role name and click Add.
    For example, ETHOS_ALL_ACCESS.
  3. Enter a description of the role.
  4. In the I/O field, select I.
  5. In the Element field, select FULLACCOUNT.
  6. In the From Value and To Value fields, enter *.
  7. Save your changes on the GLRD form.

What to do next

You can create a GL user definition and assign the GL role that has access to all general ledger accounts.
Create a GL user definition and assign the GL access role

Use the GL User Definition (GLUD) form to assign the GL access role to a user.

Before you begin

You must have already defined a GL role with access to all GL accounts.

About this task

For the user to have access to general ledger information, you need to assign the GL role that has access to all GL accounts.
User Purpose Name Example
Proxy API user or EMA Admin user Colleague needs a user to have a role that has access to all GL accounts. For a user, assign the GL role that grants access to all GL accounts. For example, ETHOS_ALL_ACCESS.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the GL User Definition (GLUD) form.
  2. At the GL User LookUp prompt, enter the operator ID for the user and click Add.
    For example, the operator ID for the Proxy API user or the EMA Admin user.
  3. Enter the Start Date for the user.
  4. Enter the GL role that has access to all GL accounts.
  5. Save your changes on the GLUD form.

Set up Colleague in Ethos Integration

In Ethos Integration, create an application for Colleague and add the resources for which Colleague is authoritative.

Create the application in Ethos Integration for Colleague

The application record in Ethos Integration contains basic information about Colleague, including the location of the Colleague Web APIs, the resources for which Colleague is the authoritative source, and the API key.

About this task

The Application Setup Wizard automatically adds ownership of Ethos resources to the application. It will get the list of resources to add by calling the /resources endpoint of the API.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, click Add Application.
  4. On the Applications page, in the Create New App area, select From Catalog.
    The catalog option automatically populates all the resources owned by Colleague based on the resources URL and credentials that you enter in the wizard.

    This option is available only for Colleague Web API 1.17 and later. If you are on an earlier version of the Colleague Web API, select Manually and complete the wizard. You will need to manually add resources later.

  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Example name: Colleague
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. On the Select Catalog Application page of the wizard, do the following:
    1. In the left pane, select Ellucian Colleague.
    2. In the right pane, enter the following information:
      Field Entry
      Base URI Enter the base URI of the Colleague Web API website, in the following form:

      https://<hostname>:<port>/ColleagueApi

      where <hostname> is the name of the web server hosting the Colleague Web API, and <port> is the port number you specified when you created the website.
      Base QAPI URI Enter the base QAPI URI of the Colleague Web API website, in the following form:

      https://<hostname>:<port>/ColleagueApi/qapi
      Username/Password Enter the username and password of a Colleague account with access to the Colleague Web API. For example, if you created the ema_admin user account and assigned the permissions recommended by Ellucian, you can enter that user's credentials here.
    3. Click Next.
  7. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, click Skip.
    Colleague does not subscribe to changes published by other Ethos applications.
  8. Click View Application if you are ready to configure application-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the application now and configure settings later.
Specify EMS settings in Colleague

Define settings that the Ellucian Message Adapter uses to link the Ellucian Messaging Service with Colleague.

About this task

This procedure covers the settings that you need to change during initial setup. For a description of the other fields on the CINC and CIIO forms, see online help.

To enter these settings, you will need the values you entered when setting up the RabbitMQ server.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague, access the Colleague Integration API Configuration (CINC) form.
  2. At the Configuration LookUp prompt, enter HUB.
    The HUB record, which is delivered by Ellucian, is required for setting up Colleague with Ethos Integration.
    Note: When you access the HUB record, Colleague defaults some of the values you defined for the INTG record on the EDX Subscriber Definition (EDSD) form.
  3. At the top of the CINC form, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    Description Enter text that describes the configuration record Ellucian Messaging Service Configuration for Ellucian Ethos Integration
    Log Level Select the maximum detail level of logging. Suggested levels:
    • DEBUG for initial setup and troubleshooting
    • ERROR during normal operation
    GUID Lifecycle Duration (sec) Specify the amount of time (in seconds) during which a data record can update one system in an integrated (shared) environment and updates can be blocked in the opposite direction. This period should be relatively short (such as 30 seconds or less) so that data update events which are triggered by regular Colleague use are not blocked from being shared with other systems.
  4. In the AMQP Message Server section, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    Use Secure Transmission Enter Y to secure transmissions sent to the Ellucian Messaging Service or N for non-secure transmissions.  
    Server Name Enter the server name on which the Ellucian Messaging Service is running. rabbitmq.mycollege.edu
    Server Port For secure transmissions, Colleague defaults port number 5671.

    For non-secure transmissions, Colleague defaults port number 5672.

    		 
    Server Base URI Displays the URI for the server on which the Ellucian Messaging Service is running.

    The URI contains the protocol, host name, and server port that the AMQP service is configured to use.

    Note: If you change the secure transmission or server values, Colleague updates the server base URI displayed.
    		 amqp://rabbitmq.​mycollege.​edu:5672
    Virtual Host Enter the RabbitMQ virtual host that you specified during Ellucian Messaging Service installation. [emsHostExample]
  5. In the Bus. Event Exchange section, specify names for the RabbitMQ topic exchange and queue for EDX.
    When you deploy the Ellucian Message Adapter and it starts for the first time, it will create this topic exchange and queue.
    Field Entry Example
    Exchange Name Specify a name for the RabbitMQ topic exchange for EDX. BusinessEventTopic
    Queue Name Specify a name for the RabbitMQ queue for the Ellucian Message Adapter. BusinessEventQueue
  6. In the Inbound/Outbound section, detail to the Colleague Integration Inbound Outbound (CIIO) form. Then, do the following:
    1. In the Use Integration Hub field, enter Y.
    2. In the Integration Hub section, enter information in the following fields:
      Note: If you are in a region other than the U.S., substitute your region-specific domain in place of integrate.elluciancloud.com in the examples. See Ethos Integration domains.
      Note: If you are whitelisting outbound traffic, configure EMA to use the static hostnames from IPs to whitelist.
      Field Entry Example
      Token URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/auth

      or

      https://tokens-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/auth      		  
      Publish URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/publish

      or

      https://messages-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/publish
      Error URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/errors

      or

      https://errors-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/errors
      Media Type Enter application/vnd.​hedtech.​change-notifications.​v2+json
    3. You can skip the AMQP section.
  7. Save your changes on the CIIO form and return to the CINC form.
  8. In the Colleague API section of the CINC form, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    EMA Admin Username Enter the username of the ema_admin user that you created in Colleague. ema_admin
  9. Save your changes on the CINC form.
  10. If this is an update to the configuration for an existing installation, restart the Ellucian Message Adapter so that the changes take effect.
Manually add resources that are owned by Colleague

If you created the Ethos application for Colleague using the option to add an application manually (rather than from the catalog), add the resources for which Colleague is the authoritative source.

About this task

Note: If you added resources when you created the application by selecting the catalog option, you can skip this procedure.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the Colleague application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. In the Authentication Type field, accept the default of Basic Authentication.
    Colleague uses basic authentication (username and password) to authenticate proxy API requests from other applications.
  6. Enter the Base URI and Base QAPI URI. If you entered those URIs previously, skip to Step 7.
    After entering each URI, click Save .
    Field Entry
    Base URI Enter the base URI of the Colleague Web API website, in the following form:

    https://<hostname>:<port>/ColleagueApi

    where <hostname> is the name of the web server hosting the Colleague Web API, and <port> is the port number you specified when you created the website.
    Base QAPI URI Enter the base QAPI URI of the Colleague Web API website, in the following form:

    https://<hostname>:<port>/ColleagueApi/qapi
  7. Click Add Resources.
  8. In the Please Select An Option dialog box, select Add Ellucian Ethos Resource(s) and then click Next.
  9. In the Add Owned Resources (Ellucian Ethos) dialog box, select the resources for which Colleague is authoritative, and then click Add.
Update Colleague's owned resources after a Colleague Web API upgrade

Update the Ethos application for Colleague with any changes to Colleague's owned resources resulting from a new version of the Colleague Web API.

About this task

Note: This option is available only for Colleague Web API 1.17 and later.
When you originally created an Ethos application for Colleague, you added the resources that Colleague owns. A new version of the Colleague Web API might include changes to the resources owned by Colleague. Perform the following procedure to update the Ethos application for Colleague with any changes to Colleague's owned resources.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the Colleague application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. Click Auto-Configure Resources.
  6. In the Request Resources from Application dialog box, enter the username and password of a Colleague account with access to the Colleague Web API. For example, if you created the ema_admin user account and assigned the permissions recommended by Ellucian, you can enter that user's credentials here.
  7. Click Next.
    The list of resources owned by Colleague is automatically updated to reflect changes in the new version of the APIs.
  8. Click Close.
    If you have not already completed your data integration parameters in Colleague, then you can do so within the administrative user interface for Ethos Integration. See Configure API settings.
Configure ISO codes for Colleague

If a Colleague application owns the ISO code configuration APIs, you can configure that application's ISO codes.

Before you begin

The minimum API release to use these features is Banner Ethos API 9.16 and Colleague Ethos API 1.24.

About this task

The application's Owned Resources page contains a link to the API Configuration ISO Code Settings page if there are ISO code resources such as countries or currencies.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. Click View Applications.
  3. Click the authoritative source application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
  5. Click Add Resources > Add Ellucian Ethos Resource(s) to add the following resources to be owned by Colleague.
    • countries
    • country-iso-codes
    • currencies
    • currency-iso-codes
    • languages
    • language-iso-codes
    • region-iso-codes
  6. Go back to the Applications landing page.
  7. On the application row, click the More icon and then click API Configuration.
    The API Configuration ISO Codes page appears. You can configure ISO codes for Country, Currency, and Language.
  8. Click Edit to change the mapping selections.
    Note: You have the option to view recommendations for ISO codes and update the configuration based on recommended values. A recommended value displays in the Recommendations column if there is an exact match.
  9. Optional: Click Credentials for Configuration to specify if you want to enter new credentials or to use the credentials provided for auto-configure resources.
  10. Optional: Click Recommendations.
    The Recommendations column populates with suggested ISO codes.
  11. Click the selections you want and click Apply, or click Apply All to apply all recommendations.
    Note: If no recommendations are available, a message states there are no recommendations.
  12. Optional: Click Export to generate an Excel spreadsheet that contains the ISO codes for all ISO code tabs on the user interface.
Set up other applications to access Colleague resources

Other applications can access Colleague resources through Ethos Integration by making proxy API requests or GraphQL requests, or by subscribing to data changes.

Setting up other applications is not part of initial setup of Colleague with Ethos Integration. Instead, you will perform these procedures when you set up the other application in Ethos Integration.

For some Ellucian applications, there are specific procedures for setup in Ethos Integration. For other applications or your own custom application, use the general procedures in Set up applications in Ethos Integration (single owner).

Person saved lists and Colleague Ethos APIs

Certain Colleague Ethos APIs provide a way to filter responses based on a set of person IDs, or a person saved list. Such an API request is made using a named query that references person-filters.

For example, when requesting a GET of all persons, the API accepts a personFilter named query and responds with the set of persons whose IDs are in the saved list. Some APIs further narrow this list based on the selection criteria for the API. For example, the list of persons returned by the personFilter named query for the students API is filtered to ignore non-students.

Below are guidelines for filtering an API using a person saved list:
  • Create and maintain person saved lists using the Person Save List Creation (SLC) form. The selection criteria and other selection parameters are stored in the SAVE.LIST.PARMS file, whereas the resulting select list is stored in the SAVEDLISTS file.
  • The person-filters API exposes the SAVE.LIST.PARMS file records, regardless of whether a saved list has been generated for a set of criteria.
  • The selection criteria captured in SAVE.LIST.PARMS are not executed when invoked as a personFilter named query during an API read operation.
  • If a SAVE.LIST.PARMS record has been defined but the selection has not been executed and stored to the SAVEDLISTS file using the Save List Name to Save Results Under field on SLC, a personFilter named query returns an empty set when used to filter an API request.
  • If a SAVE.LIST.PARMS record has been defined and the selection has already been executed, a personFilter named query uses only those keys in the saved list that refer to a person. Any corporation keys are ignored when applying a personFilter named query to the response set.

For more information, refer to Ellucian Ethos Data Model API Filtering.

Set up Colleague with Data Access

If your integration will use GraphQL requests to read Colleague data stored in Ellucian Ethos Data Access, you need to set up the loading of Colleague data into Data Access.

Install the Ellucian Messaging Service with Colleague

The Ellucian Messaging Service is message queuing software that decouples the event generator for Banner or Colleague from the software that processes the business events.

It is recommended that the Messaging Service and Messaging Adapter be installed behind a firewall.

Note: If the Messaging Service and Messaging Adapter are installed a separate server from the ERP's Web API server, the recommended server configuration is a 2 core CPU with at least 2GB of memory.
Note:

If Erlang or RabbitMQ are already installed for a prior product, they should not be re-installed. Multiple Ellucian products can and should use the same RabbitMQ installation, but you can use different installations for production and non-production environments.

However, on the CRM application servers for CRM Recruit, Ellucian installs RabbitMQ separately from any other RabbitMQ installation to be used specifically for the Ellucian Task Service for Recruit. This is used separately from Banner Event Publisher or Ethos functionality, which is the recommended usage.

Install the Ellucian Messaging Service on Windows

If you are installing the Ellucian Messaging Service with a Windows operating system, perform this procedure to download the installer and install the components.

Before you begin

If you have a previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service installed, you must uninstall it before installing a newer version. In addition, you must stop the RabbitMQ service using the Windows Services console.

Warning: Uninstalling the previous version will delete any existing message queues. Verify that all message queues are empty before uninstalling the previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service.
Warning: Uninstalling the previous version will delete the ssl directory and the rabbitmq.config file. If you have configured the previous version of the Ellucian Messaging Service for SSL, you should backup these files before uninstalling the Ellucian Messaging Service.

Install the prerequisite Microsoft® package. Go to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170 and install C and C++ (MSVC) runtime libraries.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service executable file from the Ellucian Downloads or using SA Valet.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Messaging Service that is certified with your Ethos API version. For the certified versions, see the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix or Banner Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    The file is named EllucianMessagingServicexxxSetup.exe where xxx is the version number.

  2. As an administrator, run the EllucianMessagingServicexxxSetup.exe installer to launch the install wizard.
  3. Follow the wizard prompts. In the Base Configuration Information page of the wizard, enter the following values:
    Field Description Example
    Username Username of the RabbitMQ administrative user that will be created by the install. ellucian
    Password A password for that user. rabbit
    Virtual Host Name of the RabbitMQ virtual host that will be created by the install. EllucianMessaging
    When you set up the Banner Event Publisher and enter configuration settings in the BannerEventPublisher_configuration.groovy file, you must enter this same value in the virtualHostName setting.
    • When you enter Colleague settings for Ethos Integration on the CINC form, you must enter this same value in the Virtual Host field.
    • When you enter EDX subscriber settings on the EDSD form, you must enter this same value in the virtual host part of the Subscriber Path field.

Results

The installer will perform the following actions:
  • Install Erlang and RabbitMQ.
  • Enable the RabbitMQ admin UI.
  • Configure RabbitMQ for the specified admin user.
  • Create the indicated AMQP virtual host.
Install the Ellucian Messaging Service on Linux

If you are installing the Ellucian Messaging Service with a Linux operating system, perform this procedure to download the installer and install the components.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Messaging Service that is certified with your Ethos API version. For the certified versions, see the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix or Banner Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    Ellucian provides a zip file for each supported Linux operating system. Download the file that matches your version of Linux.

    For example: Red Hat Linux 8 - EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip.

    To verify the version of Linux that is installed on the server, enter cat /etc/redhat-release.

    To verify the version of Ubuntu that is installed on the server, enter lsb_release -a.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ems.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command. Replace the EMS and Linux version numbers with the ones in your zip file.
    unzip EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip
    The extracted ZIP file will contain:
    • a ConfigureEMS shell script.
    • an Erlang RPM file.
    • a RabbitMQ RPM file.
  4. As root, install Erlang.
    For RHEL 8, enter the following commands:
    yum install erlang-23.3.4.11-1.el8.x86_64.rpm
    For Ubuntu 22.04, enter the following commands:
    dpkg -i esl-erlang_25.3.2-1~ubuntu~jammy_amd64.deb
    Note: If you receive an error that libsctp1 is a dependency, enter apt-get install libsctp1. After libsctp1 has been installed, re-run the erlang install command.
  5. As root, install RabbitMQ.
    For RHEL 8, enter the following command:
    yum install rabbitmq-server-3.9.1-1.el8.noarch.rpm
    Note: If you receive an error that socat is a dependency, enter yum install socat. After socat has been installed, re-run the RabbitMQ install command.

    For Ubuntu 22.04, enter the following commands: 

    dpkg -i rabbitmq-server_3.11.23-1_all.deb
  6. Configure AMQP and the Ellucian Messaging Service using the delivered ConfigureEMS shell script.
    1. Change permissions on the configuration script.
      chmod 700 ConfigureEMS
    2. As root, run the configuration script with its three required command line arguments.
      Syntax: ConfigureEMS username password vhostname
      Argument Description Example
      username Username of the RabbitMQ administrative user that will be created by the install. ellucian
      password A password for that user. rabbit
      vhostname Name of the RabbitMQ virtual host that will be created by the install. EllucianMessaging
      Example: ./ConfigureEMS ellucian rabbit EllucianMessaging
      When you set up the Banner Event Publisher and enter configuration settings in the BannerEventPublisher_configuration.groovy file, you must enter this same value in the virtualHostName setting.
      • When you enter Colleague settings for Ethos Integration on the CINC form, you must enter this same value in the Virtual Host field.
      • When you enter EDX subscriber settings on the EDSD form, you must enter this same value in the virtual host part of the Subscriber Path field.
Upgrade the Ellucian Messaging Service on Linux

If you have installed the with a Linux operating system, perform this procedure to upgrade it.

About this task

You may encounter errors when you upgrade because of version incompatibilities. Errors can occur when you upgrade EMS from version 7 to 8.

If you run into RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibility, and you want to preserve existing data and configuration, follow these steps Resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities when upgrading EMS.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Messaging Service ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Messaging Service that is certified with your Ethos API version. For the certified versions, see the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix or Banner Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    Ellucian provides a zip file for each supported Linux operating system. Download the file that matches your version of Linux.

    For example: Red Hat Linux 8 - EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip.

    To verify the version of Linux that is installed on the server, enter cat /etc/redhat-release.

    To verify the version of Ubuntu that is installed on the server, enter lsb_release -a.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ems.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command. Replace the EMS and RHEL version numbers with the numbers in your zip file.
    unzip EllucianMessagingService5.0-RHEL8.zip
    The extracted ZIP file will contain:
    • a ConfigureEMS shell script.
    • an Erlang RPM file.
    • a RabbitMQ RPM file.
  4. Stop the Banner Event Publisher (for Banner clients) or EDX (for Colleague clients).
    See the Banner or Colleague documentation for more information about stopping BEP or EDX.
  5. Stop the service with the following command. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
  6. As root, upgrade Erlang.
  7. As root, upgrade .
  8. Start the service with the following command. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
  9. Start BEP (for Banner clients) or EDX (for Colleague clients).
    See the Banner or Colleague documentation for more information about starting BEP or EDX.
Resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities when upgrading EMS

When you upgrade the Ellucian Messaging Service, resolve RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibilities if they occur.

About this task

Errors can occur when you upgrade EMS from version 7 to 8. If you run into RabbitMQ and Erlang incompatibility, and you want to preserve existing data and configuration, follow these steps.

Procedure

  1. Prepare a backup directory.
    1. Create a directory named backup under /home/ems. 
      sudo mkdir -p /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
    2. Set the RabbitMQ user as the owner of the directory and grant permissions to write. 
      sudo chown rabbitmq:rabbitmq /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
sudo chmod 755 /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup
  2. Export RabbitMQ configurations, messages, and definitions.
    1. Before copying any data, stop the RabbitMQ server. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
    2. Copy the mnesia directory (messages db). 
      sudo cp -r /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/mnesia.bak
    3. Copy RabbitMQ configurations. 
      sudo cp -r /etc/rabbitmq /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/rabbitmq.bak
    4. Start the RabbitMQ server to copy definitions, then execute the command export_definitions. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl export_definitions /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/definitions.json
  3. Uninstall RabbitMQ and Erlang.
    1. Stop the RabbitMQ server, then delete RabbitMQ directories. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
sudo rm -rf /etc/rabbitmq /var/lib/rabbitmq
    2. Remove RabbitMQ and Erlang from the system. 
      sudo yum remove -y erlang rabbitmq-server
  4. Upgrade RabbitMQ and Erlang .
    1. Replace the RabbitMQ and Erlang RPMs with the files included in your zip file. 
      sudo yum install -y <erlang-rpm> <rabbitmq-server-rpm>
  5. Get the node name.
    It is necessary to obtain the RabbitMQ node name to configure the server after you import the previous RabbitMQ version.
    1. Start RabbitMQ.
    2. Get the server status, which includes the name of the node from the current server instance.
    3. Store the value to configure the server later. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl status | grep "Node name"
  6. Import RabbitMQ definitions.
    1. Run the import definitions command when the server is up.
      A message displays stating that the process is asynchronous and can take some time. Watch target node logs for completion.
    2. After completion, stop the server to continue with RabbitMQ backup import 
      sudo rabbitmqctl import_definitions /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/definitions.json
sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
  7. Import RabbitMQ configurations and messages.
    1. Create a copy of /etc/rabbitmq and /var/lib/rabbitmq before you import the configurations and messages backup in case something goes wrong.
    2. Remove /etc/rabbitmq, then copy the rabbitmq.bak directory content to /etc into a new RabbitMQ directory. 
      sudo rm -rf /etc/rabbitmq
sudo cp -r /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/rabbitmq.bak/. /etc/rabbitmq
    3. Do the same with the mnesia directory. After importing mnesia, set the RabbitMQ user as owner and grant permissions to write. 
      sudo rm -rf /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo cp -r /home/ems/rabbitmq-backup/mnesia.bak/. /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo chown -R rabbitmq:rabbitmq /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
sudo chmod 755 /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia
      Before starting the RabbitMQ server, you must add feature flags to RabbitMQ to be able to start the server successfully. Edit the file /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia/<rabbitmq-node-name>-feature_flags and add the following to the array.
      stream_filtering,message_containers,stream_update_config_command
  8. Start RabbitMQ.
    1. After all imports are done, start RabbitMQ server and verify it starts up.
    2. Enable all stable feature flags to prevent unexpected behavior. 
      sudo /sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
sudo rabbitmqctl enable_feature_flag all
Configure RabbitMQ for SSL (Windows)

Install the SSL certificate, private key, and CA certificate files required to configure RabbitMQ for SSL on Windows. After performing these steps, a secure port will be set up that will accept AMQPS communications.

Before you begin

You must have three certificates files from a well-known Certificate Authority.

  • Private Key (should not be password protected)
  • Root + Intermediate Certificates
  • Server Certificate

Any intermediate certificates need to be contained in the same file as the root certificate. The server certificate should be in its own file. All of the certificate files, including the key, should be in a Base64 encoded (PEM) format. If you view them in a text editor, the file should begin and end with Begin Certificate and End Certificate or Begin RSA Private Key and End RSA Private Key.

Procedure

  1. Create an ssl directory under the installation directory to store the certificate files.

    For example, C:\Program Files\Ellucian\EllucianMessagingService\AMQP\rabbitmq_server-x.x.x\ssl

  2. Copy the two certificate files and one key file into the ssl directory.
  3. Create or edit the file: %APPDATA%\Roaming\RABBITMQ\advanced.config
  4. Add the following to the file, using the appropriate certificate names.
    Note: Backslashes ("\") in the configuration file are interpreted as an escape character. You must use "\\" or "/" when specifying file paths.
    [
  {rabbit, [
     {ssl_listeners, [5671]}, 
     {ssl_options, [{cacertfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/root_cert.pem"}, 
     {certfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/server_cert.pem"}, 
     {keyfile,"C:/Program Files/Ellucian/EllucianMessagingService/AMQP/rabbitmq_server-x.x.x/ssl/key.pem"},
     {verify,verify_peer},
     {fail_if_no_peer_cert,false}]}
]}
].
    Warning: Make sure to include a period (.) at the end of the code snippet. This period must be present.
  5. Go to the Windows Services by running services.msc. Scroll down to the RabbitMQ service, and stop the service.
  6. Click Start > All Programs > RabbitMQ > (Re)install Service.
  7. Go to the Windows Services by running services.msc. Scroll down to the RabbitMQ service, and start the service.
Configure RabbitMQ for SSL (Linux)

Install the SSL certificate, private key, and CA certificate files required to configure RabbitMQ for SSL on Linux. After performing these steps, a secure port will be set up that will accept AMQPS communications.

Before you begin

You must have three certificates files from a well-known Certificate Authority.

  • Private Key (should not be password protected)
  • Root + Intermediate Certificates
  • Server Certificate

Any intermediate certificates need to be contained in the same file as the root certificate. The server certificate should be in its own file. All of the certificate files, including the key, should be in a Base64 encoded (PEM) format. If you view them in a text editor, the file should begin and end with Begin Certificate and End Certificate or Begin RSA Private Key and End RSA Private Key.

Procedure

  1. Create an ssl directory under /etc/rabbitmq to store the certificate files.
  2. Copy the two certificate files and the one key file into the ssl directory.
  3. Create or edit the file /etc/rabbitmq/advanced.config.
  4. Add the following entries to the file, using the appropriate certificate file names. 
    [
  {rabbit, [
     {ssl_listeners, [5671]},
     {ssl_options, [
       {cacertfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/root_cert.pem"},
       {certfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/server_cert.pem"},
       {keyfile,"/etc/rabbitmq/ssl/key.pem"},
       {verify,verify_peer},
       {fail_if_no_peer_cert,false}
    ]}
  ]}
].
    Warning: Make sure to include a period (.) at the end of the code snippet. This period must be present.
  5. Restart the RabbitMQ service by running the following commands. 
    /sbin/service rabbitmq-server stop
/sbin/service rabbitmq-server start
Validate the Ellucian Messaging Service

You can use the RabbitMQ administrative interface to check that the Ellucian Messaging Service is correctly configured for Ethos Integration.

Procedure

  1. In a browser, navigate to port 15672 on the server where you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    Examples: http://localhost:15672 (from the Ellucian Messaging Service server) or http://ems.mycollege.edu:15672 (from another computer in the network)
    The URL starts with http rather than https, as shown in the examples. When you configured RabbitMQ for SSL, you secured the amqp connection, not the RabbitMQ administrative interface.
  2. At the login prompt, enter the username and password that you specified when you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    Example: Username = ellucian, password = rabbit
  3. On the Overview page, in the Listening Ports section, check that the table includes amqp::5672 and amqp/ssl::5671.
  4. Click the Admin tab, and then select Virtual Hosts.
  5. On the Virtual Hosts page, check the following:
    • The table should include a row for the virtual host whose name you specified when you installed the Ellucian Messaging Service.
    • The Users column should show that the user created during the Ellucian Messaging Service install has access to that virtual host. Example: ellucian
  6. If either the virtual host or user does not exist, you can create them:
    1. If the virtual host does not exist, click Virtual Hosts on the Admin page, and then select Add a new virtual host.
    2. If the user does not exist, click Users on the Admin page, and then select Add a user.
    3. After creating the virtual host or user, grant that user permissions on the virtual host:
      • On the Users page, click on the username to access the Permissions page.
      • Set the default .* permissions for configure, write, and read access.

Configure EDX

Colleague notifies Ellucian Ethos Integration about changes to data using Envision Data Exchange (EDX).

Set up the EDX subscriber settings

For Colleague to publish data to Ellucian Ethos Integration using the Ellucian Messaging Service, you must complete the EDX subscriber settings for the INTG subscriber.

About this task

Defining the Ellucian Messaging Service settings and enabling the subscriber allows Colleague EDX transactions to be published to Ellucian Ethos Integration.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the EDX Subscriber Definition (EDSD) form.
  2. At the Subscriber LookUp prompt, enter INTG.
  3. In the Distribution Method field, select AMQP.
  4. In the Use Secure Transmission field, enter Yes if you want to secure the transmissions between the DMI App listener and the Ellucian Messaging Service, or enter No if you do not need to secure the transmissions.
  5. Specify the username and password for the Ellucian Messaging Service in the Institution ID and Institution Password fields.
    This username and password were defined for the admin user when the Ellucian Messaging Service was installed and configured.
  6. In the Subscriber Address field, enter the DNS name where the Ellucian Messaging Service is installed.
  7. In the Subscriber Port field, enter 5672 for non-secure transmission or 5671 for secure transmission, which the Ellucian Messaging Service uses as the default port numbers.
  8. In the Subscriber Path field, enter the information below using the format shown in parentheses.
    • Exchange name (required)—(/exchange=name)—The AMQP topic exchange name Colleague uses to publish data. This exchange name must match the exchange name that you defined on the Colleague Integration API Configuration (CINC) form (for example, BusinessEventTopic).
    • Virtual host (required)—(/virtualhost=name)— The name of the virtual host that you defined when installing the Ellucian Messaging Service (for example, Ellucian Messaging).
    • Timeout (optional)—(/timeout=value)—The time, in milliseconds, that is allowed for the connection session between Colleague and the AMQP service. If you do not specify a timeout value, the default value of 0 is used, which indicates that a timeout is not enforced.

    Here is an example of an entry in the Subscriber Path field (where a timeout is not enforced):

    /virtualhost=EllucianMessaging/exchange=BusinessEventTopic

    You can enter the values for this field in any order.

  9. In the Archive field, enter Yes if you want to archive all successful transactions sent to this subscriber, or enter No if you do not want to archive all successful transactions.
    Unless you want a historical view of all successful transactions, enter Yes for test environments and No for production environments. Archived transactions can be viewed using the EDX Log (EDXL) form.
  10. In the Do you want to enable subscriber field, enter Yes.
    Note: If you change this setting from No to Yes, you must stop and restart the EDX background process using the EDQM form in UI for the subscriber to be enabled.
  11. Save your changes on the EDSD form.
Load the EDX subscriber triggers

For Colleague to send data to Ellucian Ethos Integration, you must first load the associated EDX subscriber triggers.

About this task

When you load the EDX subscriber triggers, Colleague clears any existing subscriber triggers and installs the current definitions, ensuring that you have up-to-date triggers.

For more information, see the EDX Administration manual.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the EDX Interface Load Utility (UT-EDIL) form.
  2. In the Clear all existing trigger definitions field, enter No, which ensures that the triggers for other subscribers are unaffected.
  3. In the Subscriber Interfaces to Load field, enter INTG.
  4. Save your changes on the EDIL form.
Start the EDX background process

For Colleague to send data to Ellucian Ethos Integration, you must start the EDX background process.

About this task

When the EDX background process is running, all EDX transactions for Ellucian Ethos Integration are viewable through the EDX Queue Status (EDQS) form.
Tip: If you restart the DMI listeners on the Colleague application server, the background process also stops and must be restarted. Additionally, after reloading triggers using the EDIL form, if the EDX Queue Management (EDQM) form indicates the background process is running, you must stop the process and then restart it to ensure that it is running.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the EDX Queue Management (EDQM) form.
  2. In the Action field, click Start.
  3. In the Archive field, enter Yes to archive all successful transactions, or enter No to not archive all successful transactions.
    Unless you want a historical view of all successful transactions, enter Yes for test environments and No for production environments. You can view archived transactions using the EDX Log (EDXL) form.
    Note: The Archive field setting on the EDX Subscriber Definition (EDSD) form overrides this setting.
  4. In the Alert E-mail Address field, enter the email address to which you want to send alerts for EDX transaction errors.
    Transaction errors can be viewed using the EDX Errors (EDXE) form.
  5. Save your changes on the EDQM form.
Review EDX transactions

You can view EDX and process transaction status and details. You can also use the Ellucian Messaging Service to view EDX transaction responses.

When EDX sends a message through the Ellucian Messaging Service, the service sends back one of the following message types to Colleague:
  • Success—The transaction was successful and can be viewed on the EDX Log (EDXL) form.
  • Failure—A validation error occurred and can be viewed on the EDX Errors (EDXE) form. The EDX queue continues to run normally.
  • Error—A low-level error occurred and can be viewed on the EDX Queue Status (EDQS) form. DMI will continue to connect to the subscriber up to the number of consecutive attempts specified on the EDX Queue Management (EDQM) form.
Table 1. EDX forms that monitor EDX transactions
Form Purpose
EDX Queue Status (EDQS) View a list of transactions in the EDX.STATUS file.
EDX Queue Detail (EDQD) View transaction details in the EDX.STATUS file. Access this form from the EDQS form.
EDX Errors (EDXE) View transactions in the EDX.ERR file.
EDX Error Details (EDED) View transaction details in the EDX.ERR file. Access this form from the EDXE form.
EDX Log (EDXL) View transactions in the EDX.LOG file.
EDX Log Detail (EDLD) View transaction details in the EDX.LOG file. Access this form from the EDXL form.
Resolve errors when sending Colleague data

If you experience issues when sending data from Colleague to the Ellucian Messaging Service, you must resolve the issues. Data sent from Colleague to the Ellucian Messaging Service uses Envision Data Exchange (EDX).

Error Resolution
Trigger is not being executed. Run the EDX Interface Load Utility (EDIL) process for the INTG subscriber (do not clear all existing trigger definitions) to update the RFSPECS records for affected Colleague files with the trigger information.
Trigger is being executed but data is still not being sent to the Ellucian Messaging Service. Access the EDX Subscriber Definition (EDSD) form for the INTG subscriber, and determine whether the correct subscriber address, port, and path were entered.
Transaction appears on the EDX Queue Status (EDQS) form as an error and shuts down the subscriber. The error message shown on the EDX Queue Detail (EDQD) form from the transaction attempt is "Listener failed to respond." Confirm that the Ellucian Messaging Service is running on the server that is defined on the EDSD form. Confirm that there is enough disk space on that server for a successful transaction.
Transaction has a New status on the EDX Queue Status (EDQS) form and has not been processed. Access the EDX Queue Management (EDQM) form and ensure that the EDX background process is running. If there are other transactions ahead of this one that have an Error status, then the subscriber may have been disabled for having too many errors.

Fix the cause of the errors, and then check the EDSD form to ensure that the INTG subscriber is Active. If it has been disabled, enable the subscriber and go to the EDQM form to halt and restart the EDX background process.
Enable and disable Ethos EDX triggers

You can turn on (enable) or turn off (disable) EDX triggers for Ethos resources based on the needs of your subscribing systems.

About this task

Starting with Colleague Web API 1.29, EDX triggers for new Ethos resources are delivered disabled. If your subscribing systems require any of the new resources, you must enable the EDX triggers for those resources. If your system does not rely on the use of these resources, it is not necessary to enable the new triggers.

EDX triggers for existing Ethos resources are enabled by default. You can use the Enable/Disable control on the CIMC form in addition to trigger conditions of the business events checking for a user-specified "1" EQ "0" to turn off EDX triggers. To disable EDX triggers, use the CIMC form and update the Action to Disable. Then detail from the business event to the Colleague Integration Trigger Conditions (CITC) form and detail from there to the EDX Trigger Conditions (EDTC) form to remove any "1" EQ "0" conditions. Alternatively, you can leave the "1" EQ "0" conditions in place. However, if you want to then change the resource EDX triggers to enable, you must update the Action to Enable on the CIMC form AND remove any "1" EQ "0" conditions for the EDX Triggers to work properly.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague UI, access the Colleague Integration API Configuration (CINC) form
  2. At the Configuration LookUp prompt, enter HUB.
  3. From the Mapping field, access the Integration API Mapping Configuration (CIMC) form.
  4. On the CIMC form, use the Set All Actions and the Action field for each resource to enable or disable all or specific EDX triggers.
  5. Triggers that have been disabled using a trigger condition such as WITH "1" EQ "0" or a similar construct are displayed on CIMC with a status of Enabled. To remove this workaround so that you can manage Ethos EDX triggers using the CIMC form, complete the following steps:
    1. From the Business Event(s) field, access the Colleague Integration Trigger Conditions (CITC) form.
    2. On the CITC form, access EDX Trigger Conditions (EDTC) form for each trigger condition.
    3. On the EDTC form, remove the workaround.
    4. Return to the CIMC form and disable the trigger if you want it to remain disabled.

Specify EMS settings in Colleague

Define settings that the Ellucian Message Adapter uses to link the Ellucian Messaging Service with Colleague.

About this task

This procedure covers the settings that you need to change during initial setup. For a description of the other fields on the CINC and CIIO forms, see online help.

To enter these settings, you will need the values you entered when setting up the RabbitMQ server.

Procedure

  1. In Colleague, access the Colleague Integration API Configuration (CINC) form.
  2. At the Configuration LookUp prompt, enter HUB.
    The HUB record, which is delivered by Ellucian, is required for setting up Colleague with Ethos Integration.
    Note: When you access the HUB record, Colleague defaults some of the values you defined for the INTG record on the EDX Subscriber Definition (EDSD) form.
  3. At the top of the CINC form, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    Description Enter text that describes the configuration record Ellucian Messaging Service Configuration for Ellucian Ethos Integration
    Log Level Select the maximum detail level of logging. Suggested levels:
    • DEBUG for initial setup and troubleshooting
    • ERROR during normal operation
    GUID Lifecycle Duration (sec) Specify the amount of time (in seconds) during which a data record can update one system in an integrated (shared) environment and updates can be blocked in the opposite direction. This period should be relatively short (such as 30 seconds or less) so that data update events which are triggered by regular Colleague use are not blocked from being shared with other systems.
  4. In the AMQP Message Server section, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    Use Secure Transmission Enter Y to secure transmissions sent to the Ellucian Messaging Service or N for non-secure transmissions.  
    Server Name Enter the server name on which the Ellucian Messaging Service is running. rabbitmq.mycollege.edu
    Server Port For secure transmissions, Colleague defaults port number 5671.

    For non-secure transmissions, Colleague defaults port number 5672.

    		 
    Server Base URI Displays the URI for the server on which the Ellucian Messaging Service is running.

    The URI contains the protocol, host name, and server port that the AMQP service is configured to use.

    Note: If you change the secure transmission or server values, Colleague updates the server base URI displayed.
    		 amqp://rabbitmq.​mycollege.​edu:5672
    Virtual Host Enter the RabbitMQ virtual host that you specified during Ellucian Messaging Service installation. [emsHostExample]
  5. In the Bus. Event Exchange section, specify names for the RabbitMQ topic exchange and queue for EDX.
    When you deploy the Ellucian Message Adapter and it starts for the first time, it will create this topic exchange and queue.
    Field Entry Example
    Exchange Name Specify a name for the RabbitMQ topic exchange for EDX. BusinessEventTopic
    Queue Name Specify a name for the RabbitMQ queue for the Ellucian Message Adapter. BusinessEventQueue
  6. In the Inbound/Outbound section, detail to the Colleague Integration Inbound Outbound (CIIO) form. Then, do the following:
    1. In the Use Integration Hub field, enter Y.
    2. In the Integration Hub section, enter information in the following fields:
      Note: If you are in a region other than the U.S., substitute your region-specific domain in place of integrate.elluciancloud.com in the examples. See Ethos Integration domains.
      Note: If you are whitelisting outbound traffic, configure EMA to use the static hostnames from IPs to whitelist.
      Field Entry Example
      Token URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/auth

      or

      https://tokens-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/auth      		  
      Publish URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/publish

      or

      https://messages-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/publish
      Error URL Enter https://integrate.​elluciancloud.​com/errors

      or

      https://errors-static.integration.elluciancloud.com/errors
      Media Type Enter application/vnd.​hedtech.​change-notifications.​v2+json
    3. You can skip the AMQP section.
  7. Save your changes on the CIIO form and return to the CINC form.
  8. In the Colleague API section of the CINC form, enter the following values:
    Field Entry Example
    EMA Admin Username Enter the username of the ema_admin user that you created in Colleague. ema_admin
  9. Save your changes on the CINC form.
  10. If this is an update to the configuration for an existing installation, restart the Ellucian Message Adapter so that the changes take effect.

The Ellucian Message Adapter publishes data changes from Colleague to Ellucian Ethos Integration. Perform these procedures to configure the Ellucian Message Adapter and then deploy it to either a Tomcat web server.

WebLogic is no longer supported as a web server.

EMA Java requirements:

EMA version Minimum Java version, compatible with version
5.0 11
5.1 and 5.2 Minimum 8, compatible with 11
5.3 Minimum 17
5.3.1 Minimum 17, compatible with 21
5.4.0 Minimum 17, compatible with 21

Define the EMA_CONFIG encryption key

The Ellucian Message Adapter uses the EMA_CONFIG encryption key to encrypt and decrypt sensitive information stored in the emsConfig.xml file.

Use the appropriate procedure for your web server to define the encryption key.

(Tomcat) Create the EMA_CONFIG environment variable

Perform this procedure if you are using the Tomcat web server.

About this task

If you previously created the EMA_CONFIG environment variable for an earlier version of the Ellucian Message Adapter, you can skip this procedure.

Procedure

  1. Create a user or system environment variable.
    If you create a user environment variable, it must be for the user that is running your web server.
    1. For the variable name, enter EMA_CONFIG
    2. For the variable value, enter any text string.
      This text string is the encryption key.
  2. Stop and restart the Tomcat web server.
Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter

Enter values in the configuration file that the Ellucian Message Adapter uses to communicate with the Ethos APIs and other Ellucian Ethos Integration components.

You will download the EMA zip file to a Windows or Linux server. The zip file includes a WAR file which contains the emsConfig.xml configuration file where you will enter the settings.

Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter on Windows with Colleague

If you are installing the Ellucian Message Adapter zip file on a Windows server, perform this procedure to enter the configuration settings.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Message Adapter ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads or using SA Valet.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Message Adapter that is certified with your Ethos API version. See the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    The ZIP file is named EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip where x.x.x is the version number.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as C:\ellucian\EMA.
  3. Unzip the EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip file.
    The ZIP file contains:
    • Ellucian Messaging Adapter WAR file.
    • emsConfig.template xml configuration file.
    • ConfigureEMS.bat batch file for Windows.
    • ConfigureEMS.sh shell script for Linux.
  4. Double click ConfigureEMS.bat to configure the Ellucian Message Adapter WAR file.
    Note: Do not right-click and select Run as administrator.
  5. If prompted, enter the directory path to where JAVA is installed.
    A Notepad window opens and displays the emsConfig.xml file.
  6. Enter the configuration settings.
    For guidance, see the configuration settings topic for your scenario:
    • EMA configuration settings for Banner (MEP - single tenant)
    • EMA configuration settings for Colleague
    Note: If this is an upgrade from an earlier version of the Ellucian Message Adapter, you can copy some of the values from the existing emsConfig.xml file contained in the Ellucian Message Adapter WAR file that is currently deployed.
  7. Save your changes to the configuration file and close the text editor.
    The batch process updates the WAR file with the changes to the configuration file.

Results

The WAR file is now ready for deployment.
Configure the Ellucian Message Adapter on Linux with Colleague

If you are installing the Ellucian Message Adapter zip file on a Linux server, perform this procedure to enter the configuration settings.

Procedure

  1. Download the Ellucian Message Adapter ZIP file from the Ellucian Downloads or using SA Valet.

    Download the latest version of Ellucian Message Adapter that is certified with your Ethos API version. See the Colleague Ethos API compatibility matrix, available as an attachment from the Ellucian Ethos support information page.

    The ZIP file is named EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip where x.x.x is the version number.

  2. Place the zip file in an empty directory such as /home/ema.
  3. Unzip the zip file using the following command. Replace x.x.x with your version number, such as 5.0.0.
    unzip EllucianMessagingAdapterx.x.x.zip
  4. Change to the subdirectory that contains the unzipped files (replace x.x.x with your version number):

    The ZIP file contains:
