Add GraphQL resources to an application (single owner)

Set up an application to make GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access, in an environment where each resource is owned by just one application.

About this task

Note the following about setting up GraphQL requests:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add GraphQL resources to an existing Ethos application. You can also add GraphQL resources when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required resources when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to this procedure performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the requesting application to make a GraphQL request to Ethos Integration. See Make GraphQL requests to Data Access.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the GraphQL Resources tab.
  5. Click Add Resources.
  6. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
  7. Click Add.
    In this case, if you add a resource and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will not be available for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.
  8. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, see Grant access to resource configurations your tenant owns.
Remove GraphQL resources from an application (single owner)

You can remove GraphQL resources from an application that makes GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access, in an environment where each resource is owned by just one application.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the GraphQL Resources tab.
  5. Click Delete , then Yes, Delete to confirm.
    In this case, if you remove a resource and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will still be accessible for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the "reset-cache" header. This header set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.

Set up applications in Ethos Integration (multiple owners)

Create the Ethos Integration applications, and set up resources, subscriptions, proxy API requests, and GraphQL requests, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

For each Ethos data model, there is generally one application that is logically responsible for maintaining the data in the data model. However, in some cases, multiple applications, or multiple instances of an application, maintain the same data.

Create authentication credentials for proxy API requests

If your software application will make proxy API requests to another software application, you need to set up a user or token in the target application to support authentication of the requests.

You will enter the user credentials or token when you set up proxy API requests in the requesting application, which you can do either in the Add Application wizard or later by editing the application.

Types of authentication

Through Ethos Integration, one software application (the requesting application) can make a proxy API request to access data in another software application (the target application). The request uses either of the following types of authentication to assure the target application that the requesting application can be trusted:
  • Basic authentication - The request includes credentials for a user that you create in the target software application and that has the required permissions to create/read/update/delete data in the target application. For example, proxy API requests to Banner or Colleague use basic authentication.
  • User-defined authentication - The request includes a token or API key that you create in the target software application.

Example

Assume that you have implemented a campus card system that needs to be able to read housing assignment data stored in Colleague. In this example, the campus card system is the requesting software application and Colleague is the target software application. You would do the following:
  • In Ethos Integration, create an Ethos application for Colleague, and ensure that Colleague owns the housing-assignments resource. (This resource is added automatically if you create the Colleague application from the catalog.)
  • In Colleague, create a Colleague user with READ permissions on the housing-assignments resource.
  • In Ethos Integration, create an Ethos application for the campus card system, and enter username and password for that Colleague user.
Create a user for proxy API requests with basic authentication

If your application will make proxy API requests using basic authentication, set up a user in the target application.

Procedure

  1. In the target software application (the application that owns the resources), create a user with the required permissions to access the data models needed by the requesting software application.
    If the target application is Banner or Colleague, see:
    • For Banner, see the Banner Ethos APIs section of the Ellucian API Documentation. In the information for Ellucian Ethos Data Model APIs, go to the appropriate domain (such as Foundation APIs or Student APIs) for the data model, and then go to the Security Overview section to see the required permissions.
    • For Colleague, see Create Colleague users for proxy API requests.
      Note: Some data models do not require that permissions be assigned in Colleague. For example, the Colleague user can read academic-periods information without having specific permissions assigned. If a data model does not have permissions listed in the Colleague documentation, then you do not need to assign permissions for that data model.
  2. In Ethos Integration, access the Application Overview page for the target application and confirm that:
    • The authentication type is Basic Authentication.
    • The application owns the Ethos resources that the requesting application needs to access.
Create a token for proxy API requests with user-defined authentication

If your application will make proxy API requests using user-defined authentication, set up a token or API key in the target application.

Procedure

  1. In the target software application, define the token or API key.
  2. In Ethos Integration, access the Application Overview page for the target application and confirm that:
    • The authentication type is User-Defined Authentication.
    • The application owns the Ethos resources that the requesting application needs to access.
Create the applications in Ethos Integration (multiple owners)

Each instance of a software application that participates in Ethos Integration requires an Ethos application.

Before you begin

The Add Application wizard prompts you for information about the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for this application. Before you run the wizard, determine the needs of this application:
  • If this application needs to make proxy API requests to another application, create a user or token in the target application for authentication of those requests. See Create authentication credentials for proxy API requests.
  • If this application needs to make GraphQL requests to Data Access, determine the resources that this application needs to access using those requests.
  • If this application needs to subscribe to data changes published by another application, determine the resources to which this application needs to subscribe.

About this task

Use this procedure to create an Ethos application for each instance of a software application that will participate in Ethos Integration. In a typical multi-owner scenario, you would create an Ethos application for each instance of the software application that owns resources, and an Ethos application for each instance of the software application that accesses that data through proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions.

This procedure uses the Add Application wizard to manually create an Ethos application and set up the proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions for the application. Other options for performing these functions are:
  • For some Ellucian applications, including Banner and Colleague, you can select the application from a catalog, which automatically configures the appropriate owned resources and subscriptions. See the product-specific documentation for setting up each Ellucian application in Ethos Integration to determine whether the catalog method is supported and to see the procedure.
  • You can set up or modify proxy API requests, GraphQL requests, and subscriptions by editing the application after you create it.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. In the Create New App area, click Manually.
  4. In the Add Application dialog box, do the following:
    1. If this application will make proxy API requests to retrieve data from another application, select Configure REST API proxy.
    2. If this application will make GraphQL requests to retrieve data from Data Access, select Configure GraphQL resources.
    3. Click Continue.
  5. On the Add Application page of the wizard, enter the information described below and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter a unique name for this application.

    Make sure that the name uniquely identifies this application. When you need to select an application elsewhere in the Ethos Integration user interface, you will use the name to select the correct application.
    Description (Optional) Enter a description of this application.
  6. If you selected Configure REST API proxy in the first step of the wizard, set up proxy API requests on the Add Source Applications page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Source Application to open the Add Source Application dialog box.
    2. In the Source application field, select the target application (for example, Banner or Colleague).
    3. If the target application uses basic authentication, enter the username and password for the user account that you created in the target software application.
    4. In the Select a resource field, select any Ethos resource to which that user account has permissions in the integrated solution. For example, persons.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in the ERP or other integrated solution. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    5. If the target application uses user-defined authentication, enter the token or API key that you defined in the target software application.
    6. Click Add.
    7. Repeat Steps 6.a through 6.f for each target application to which this application will make proxy API requests.
    8. If a Select Routing section of the page is displayed, select the desired source application for proxy API requests from the application you are configuring.
      The Select Routing section is displayed if you add multiple source applications, and some resources are owned by more than one of those applications.
    9. Click Next.
  7. If you selected Configure GraphQL resources in the first step of the wizard, set up GraphQL requests on the Add Resources page of the wizard:
    1. Click Add Resources.
    2. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
      If you entered credentials for source applications (Step 6), only the resources owned by those source applications are available for selection. If not, all resources owned by any application in this environment are available.
    3. Click Add.
    4. If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data through GraphQL requests, and then click Add.
      If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for GraphQL requests have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
    5. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, continue with the next step. Otherwise, click Next and skip to Step 8.
      For example, you might have loaded persons data into Data Access from Banner or Colleague. You want this application to be able to access most persons information, but not the dateOfBirth property. You would add the persons resource and then use the steps below to hide the dateOfBirth property.
      Note: For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example attribute filters for GraphQL resources.
    6. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to hide, and then click Show more .
    7. In the Attribute Filters area, click the Add icon.
    8. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to hide.
      For example, to hide the date of birth property in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

    9. If you want the property to be hidden from this application only under certain conditions, click Add Criteria and then enter the criteria:
      Field Entry
      Property Path Enter the path to the data model property to be used in the criterion. This property must be in the same resource as the property that you are hiding.
      Operator Select equals or not equals
      Criteria Enter the value of this property that will determine whether the criterion is met.
    10. Click Next.
    In this case, if you add a resource and you select a source application, the resource will not be effective for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header needs to be set to any value, and ensures that the process will not take 30 minutes.
  8. On the Add Subscriptions page of the wizard, perform the steps below if you want this application to subscribe to data changes published by another Ethos application.
    If this application does not subscribe to data changes, click Skip.
    1. Click Add Subscriptions.
    2. In the Add Subscriptions dialog box, select the resources to which this application should subscribe, and then click Add.
    3. In the Select Resource Owner area of the page, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data changes.
      If a list of applications is displayed in the Select Resource Owner area, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for subscription have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
    4. Click Next.
    In this case, if you add a resource and you select a source application, the resource will not be effective for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header needs to be set to any value, and ensures that the process will not take 30 minutes.
  9. Click View Application if you are ready to configure application-specific settings, or click Back to Applications if you want to just create the application now and configure settings later.
Set up owned resources (multiple owners)

Specify the resources that are owned by each application, and specify the default owner for resources that are owned by multiple applications.

Add owned resources to applications (multiple owners)

Specify the resources that each application owns, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

Before you begin

You need to create the application records in Ethos Integration before using this procedure to add owned resources to the applications.

About this task

Note: An application needs to own a resource only if it is authoritative for that resource, meaning that it publishes data changes and has an API to respond to proxy API requests for that resource. Do not add an owned resource to an application that accesses data for that resource through subscriptions, proxy API requests, or GraphQL requests.

Ellucian recommends that you assign resources first to the application that you expect will receive the most proxy API requests. This limits the need to change default ownership and create resource requests, as described in Change the default owner of a resource.

Using this procedure, you will add owned resources by individually selecting resources. For some Ellucian applications, when you create the application, you can select the Ellucian application from a catalog and automatically add all owned resources. See the product-specific documentation for setting up each Ellucian application in Ethos Integration to determine whether that option is supported and to see the procedure.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    Major versions of the resources display. An asterisk displays in the Major Versions column if a resource is deprecated. If you do not see versions listed next to the resources, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
  5. In the Authentication Type field, select the authentication type for proxy API requests to this application.
    Each proxy API request must include user credentials or other information so that this application (the target application) knows that the application making the proxy API request (the requesting application) can be trusted.
    • Select Basic Authentication (the default) if you want the proxy API request from the requesting application to include the username and password of a user.
    • Select User-Defined Authentication if you want the proxy API request from the requesting application to include some other information, such as a token or API key.
    Later, you will do the following:
    • Create the user, or define the other information, in the target application.
    • Enter the user credentials or other information in the Ethos application for the requesting application.
  6. Enter the Base URI and Base QAPI URI. If you entered those URIs previously, skip to Step 7.
    After entering each URI, click Save .
    Field Entry
    Base URI Enter the default location at which all of the APIs for this application reside.
    Base QAPI URI If this application supports query by POST, enter the QAPI endpoint URI.
  7. Click Add Resources.
  8. To add resources defined by Ellucian, perform the following steps.
    1. In the Please Select An Option dialog box, select Add Ellucian Ethos Resource(s) and then click Next.
    2. In the Add Owned Resources (Ellucian Ethos) dialog box, select the resources for which this application is authoritative, and then click Add.
  9. To add custom resources, perform the following steps.
    1. In the Please Select An Option dialog box, select Add A Custom Resource and then click Next.
    2. In the Add Owned Resources (Custom) dialog box, in the Resource Name field, enter a name for the custom resource.
    3. Optional: Enter a URI Override or QAPI URI Override.
      The Base URI plus the resource name is the default URI for accessing the resource. If you have customized the resource or are using a different server, you can override the default URI.
      For example, if you customized the persons resource, you might override the default URI to: http://baseuri/custom/persons.
    4. Click Add.
    5. Repeat Steps 9.a through 9.d for each custom resource that you want to add.
  10. Click More to view the following options:
    Field Description
    Override URI Use this to override the base URI.
    API Details Displays details about Ethos Data Model resources. Select Show Alternative Representations to view an additional or alternative representation in addition to the default. If you receive a 400 error, verify that your Base URI and credentials are correct and try to view the information again.
    Health Details Displays the Health Check window that determines the health of a resource. Refer to Resources Health Check.
    Configure Events Displays if Ethos applications for Banner have any events that are associated with a resource owned by Banner. See Enable events associated with Banner-owned resources.
    Note: API Details and Health Details are hidden if they are not owned resources, or if they are Data Access resources, custom resources, or another type of non-owned resources.
Change the default owner of a resource

When multiple applications own a resource, the resource has a default owner. The first application to which you add the resource becomes the initial default owner. Use this procedure if you want to change the default owner.

About this task

Proxy API requests for a resource go to the default owner unless you create a resource request using the procedure in Create a resource request to route proxy API requests (multiple owners).

To limit the need to change default ownership and create resource requests, follow these practices:
  • Add resources first to the application that you expect will receive the most proxy API requests.
  • If, for a particular resource, you expect that most proxy API requests will go to an application other than the one to which you first added the resource, change the default owner using the procedure below.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Resources.
  3. On the All Resources page, locate the resource whose default owner you want to change.
    The Resource Owner column displays all Ethos Integration applications that own the resource. If necessary, click View all resource owners to see the full list of applications that own the resource.
  4. Select the Ethos Integration application that you want to be the default owner of the resource.
Add subscriptions to an application (multiple owners)

Set up an application to access data in another application by subscribing to published data changes, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

Note the following about setting up subscriptions:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add subscriptions to an existing Ethos application. You can also add subscriptions when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required subscriptions when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to these procedures performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the subscribing software application to retrieve change notifications from Ethos Integration. See Retrieve messages.
You can add subscriptions to an existing Ethos application in two ways:
  • Add by Resource Name - Resources are listed alphabetically and can be selected one-by-one. Adding by resource name is the ideal method when it is only necessary to add a few subscriptions and you know the resource names.
  • Add by Resource Owner - Resources are listed based on the application that is configured to own them in Ethos Integration (an authoritative application). Selecting the authoritative application populates the list with all the resources that application is set up to own. You can add subscriptions to one, some, or all of the resources. Adding by resource owner is the ideal method when multiple authoritative applications share ownership over the same sets of resources, such as in a Banner Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) environment.
Add subscriptions by resource name (multiple owners)

Use these instructions to add subscriptions by resource name.

Before you begin

Before adding subscriptions to an application, you need to do the following:
  • Create the application records in Ethos Integration for the subscribing applications.
  • Make sure that all resources to which this application will subscribe are owned by another application in Ethos Integration.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Resource Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Subscriptions.
    The Add Subscriptions dialog box opens with the Add by Resource Name tab selected by default.
  6. Select the resources for which you want the application to subscribe to change notifications.
    For any resources that have multiple owners, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data changes.
  7. After you select all the desired subscriptions, click Add.
  8. If you do not want all messages published and want to subscribe to specific data, you can consume only the messages you want by setting up filter criteria. Unnecessary messages will not be saved to your queues.
    If the application has no filters set up, the application will receive all messages for the resources to which it subscribes. All published messages will be saved to your queues.
    For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example subscription filters.
    1. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to apply a filter to, and click Show more at the right end of the row.
    2. In the Filters area, click Add .
    3. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to show. For example, to get change notifications for students with a date of birth of 1984, in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth. You can add filters for more than one property in a resource.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

      Field Entry
      Path The path to the property in the JSON contents of a resource.
      Operator The operator to use for evaluating the filter - equals, not equals, exists, or contains.
      Value The value of the property to evaluate using the operator (not applicable if operator is “exists”).
    4. After defining all filters for this resource, click Save.
Add subscriptions by resource owner (multiple owners)

Use these instructions to add subscriptions by resource owner.

Before you begin

Before adding subscriptions to an application, you need to do the following:
  • Create the application records in Ethos Integration for the subscribing applications.
  • Make sure that all resources to which this application will subscribe are owned by another application in Ethos Integration.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Resource Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Subscriptions.
    The Add Subscriptions dialog box opens with the Add by Resource Name tab selected by default.
  6. Click the Add by Resource Owner tab.
  7. Select the authoritative application that owns the resources to which the applications should subscribe.
    The right side of the table populates with the resources that the selected authoritative application owns.
  8. Select the resources to which this application will subscribe. Use the Select All button to select all the resources listed. Use the Search field to search the list of Owned Resources of the authoritative application to find specific ones.
    Note: If you filter the list of resources by entering criteria in the Search field and then click Select All, you will not just add subscriptions to the resources displayed in the filtered list. You will be selecting all the resources owned by the corresponding authoritative application, even though they have been filtered from view.
  9. After you select all the desired subscriptions, click Add.
  10. If you do not want all messages published and want to subscribe to specific data, you can consume only the messages you want by setting up filter criteria. Unnecessary messages will not be saved to your queues.
    If the application has no filters set up, the application will receive all messages for the resources to which it subscribes. All published messages will be saved to your queues.
    For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example subscription filters.
    1. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to apply a filter to, and click Show more at the right end of the row.
    2. In the Filters area, click Add .
    3. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to show. For example, to get change notifications for students with a date of birth of 1984, in the persons resource, you would enter /dateOfBirth. You can add filters for more than one property in a resource.

      To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version/product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section, and expand to view properties.

      Field Entry
      Path The path to the property in the JSON contents of a resource.
      Operator The operator to use for evaluating the filter - equals, not equals, exists, or contains.
      Value The value of the property to evaluate using the operator (not applicable if operator is “exists”).
    4. After defining all filters for this resource, click Save.
Set up proxy API requests (multiple owners)

Set up an application to access data in another application using proxy API requests, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

Add credentials for proxy API requests

Add the credentials that this software application will use to make proxy API requests to another software application.

Before you begin

Before performing this procedure, you need to do the following:
  • In Ethos Integration, create Ethos applications for both the requesting software application and the target software application, if they do not yet exist.
  • Create a user (for basic authentication), or a token or API key (for user-defined authentication), in the target software application. For more information about those authentication types, and the procedures for creating the user or token, see Create authentication credentials for proxy API requests.
  • In Ethos Integration, ensure that the target software application owns the required Ethos resources, and that the authentication type is correct (Basic Authentication or User-Defined Authentication).

About this task

Note the following about setting up proxy API requests:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add credentials to an existing Ethos application. You can also add credentials when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required credentials when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to this procedure performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the requesting application to make a GET, PUT, POST, or DELETE request to Ethos Integration. See Use the Proxy API service.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the application name for the requesting software application.
  4. On the page, click the Credentials tab.
  5. Click Add Credentials.
  6. In the Add Credentials dialog box, enter the settings below.
    Field Entry
    Source application Select the Ethos application for your ERP or other integrated solution, such as Banner Integration API, Banner Student API, or Colleague.
    Username Enter the username and password for the user account you created in the integrated solution.
    Password
    Select a resource In the Select a resource field, select any Ethos resource to which that user account has permissions in the integrated solution.
    You can select any resource for which you granted that user account permissions in the integrated solution. Typical examples:
    • Banner Integration API: persons
    • Banner Student API: sections
    • Colleague Web API: persons or sections

    Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in the ERP or other integrated solution. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
  7. In the dialog box, click Add Credentials.
  8. Repeat steps 6 and 7 for each target application to which this application will make proxy API requests.
Create a resource request to route proxy API requests (multiple owners)

If this application makes proxy API calls to multiple target applications, and some resources are owned by more than one of those target applications, create resource requests to select the appropriate target application.

Before you begin

Before creating resource requests, you must add credentials for all target applications to which this application will make proxy API requests. The Request Routing page displays only those resources that are owned by applications for which you have added credentials.

About this task

Note: Using these procedures, you will manually add resource requests to an existing Ethos application. You can also add resource requests when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard, using the Select Routing feature of the wizard.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application that will make the proxy API requests.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Request Routing tab.
    The Request Routing page provides two options for creating resource requests:
    • Use the Manage by Resource Name option to specify resource requests one-by-one, selecting the desired owning application for each resource. This option is useful if there are just a small number of resources for which you want to route proxy API requests to an application other than the default owner.
    • Use the Manage by Resource Owner option to route all requests from your requesting application to a particular owning application. This option is useful if your requesting application will make all of its proxy API calls to an owning application that is not the default owner of the required resources. This is the situation in the example provided above.
  5. If you want to specify resource requests one-by-one, do the following:
    1. Click the Manage by Resource Name tab.
    2. Locate the resources for which you want to create a resource request.
      The table displays all owners of each resource. If necessary, click View all resource owners to see the full list of applications that own the resource.
    3. For each resource, select the authoritative Ethos Integration application that you want to be the target of proxy API requests from this requesting application.
  6. If you want to route all of your resource requests to a particular owning application, do the following:
    1. Click the Manage by Resource Owner tab.
    2. In the left pane, select the application that you want to be the target of proxy API requests from this requesting application.
      This list includes all Ethos Integration applications that own any resources that have multiple owners.
    3. In the Owned Resources table, select the resources for which you want to create a resource request. Click Select All if you want all proxy API calls from your application to go to the selected owning application.
Add GraphQL resources to an application (multiple owners)

Set up an application to make GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

About this task

Note the following about setting up GraphQL requests:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add GraphQL resources to an existing Ethos application. You can also add GraphQL resources when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required resources when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to this procedure performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the requesting application to make a GraphQL request to Ethos Integration. See Make GraphQL requests to Data Access.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the GraphQL Resources tab.
  5. Click Add Resources.
  6. In the Add Resources dialog box, select the resources for which this application should make GraphQL requests to Data Access.
  7. Click Add.
    In this case, if you add a resource and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will not be available for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.
  8. If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, select the owning Ethos application from which this application should get data through GraphQL requests, and then click Add.
    If the Select Source Application dialog box displays, it indicates that at least some of the resources that you have selected for GraphQL requests have multiple owners. You need to select the owning application that is associated with the application you are now configuring.
  9. If you want to prevent this application from accessing certain properties within an added resource, see Grant access to resource configurations your tenant owns.
Remove GraphQL resources from an application (multiple owners)

You can remove GraphQL resources from an application that makes GraphQL requests to Ellucian Ethos Data Access, in an environment where some resources are owned by multiple applications.

About this task

Note the following about setting up GraphQL requests:
  • Using these procedures, you will manually add GraphQL resources to an existing Ethos application. You can also add GraphQL resources when you create an Ethos application using the Add Application wizard. If you added the required resources when you ran the wizard, you can skip this procedure.
  • In addition to this procedure performed in Ethos Integration, you need to configure the requesting application to make a GraphQL request to Ethos Integration. See Make GraphQL requests to Data Access.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and then click the application name.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the GraphQL Resources tab.
  5. Click Delete , then Yes, Delete to confirm.
    In this case, if you remove a resource and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will still be accessible for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the "reset-cache" header. This header set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.

Subscribe to business events

You can update an application to add event subscriptions.

About this task

A business-event is an event that happened in the source system. It shows what event happened and what changed as a result of the event, such as an update to a person's name.

A business-event is not tied to an owned resource that is exposed through an authoritative application's API, like change-notifications are.

The content of a business-event does not have a full representation of any data model that subscribers can then copy into their system. It is more based around the event that occurred in the source system. The content contains details about what exactly was changed, and it may contain before and after values for comparison.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. Click View Applications.
  3. Click the subscriber application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Event Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Event.
    The Add Events page displays.
  6. Select an existing application from your tenant.
  7. Manually enter an Event Name.
  8. Click Add.
    When you update an application to add event subscriptions, they are saved in the eventSubscriptions array of the applications schema.
  9. Optional: To delete an event, select an event in the Event column and click Delete . To delete all events, click Delete All Events.

Grant access to resources your tenant owns

As a grantor, you can share resources that are owned by applications in your tenant and configure the credentials that will be used by that tenant for API requests.

About this task

After a grantor provides access, the applications in the grantee tenants are automatically granted permissions to make GraphQL queries on the resource from the grantor tenant.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the application name.
  4. Click the Tenant Access tab.
    Note: The number of tenants with access displays on the tab name.
  5. Under Grant Access To Other Tenants, click Add Tenant.
  6. Select a tenant from the Tenant drop-down menu.
  7. Enter the tenant's details and resources for which you are enabling read access and click Add.
    Note: You can edit and delete tenants and their credentials and modify shared resources on the Tenant Access tab.

Tenant access terms

Some common terms are defined as they relate to cross-tenant request behavior.

Term Description
Tenant A tenant environment. This refers to a tenant as it is viewed by the Tenant Management System, where each tenant environment is a separate tenant with its own ID. For example, "Ellucian University - Test" and "Ellucian University - Production" are separate tenants that belong to the same account.
Cross-tenant request A request from an application to get data from a different tenant than the one where the requesting application resides.
Grantor tenant A tenant that is granting access to some of its resources to another tenant.
Grantee tenant A tenant that is granted access to some resources of another tenant's data.
Owning application An authoritative application that owns resources.
Client application An application that is making resource requests for another tenant, either through proxy API requests or GraphQL requests.
Subscribing application An application that is subscribing to changes for resources from another tenant.

Select resources shared with your tenant to query using GraphQL requests

As a grantee, you can select resources that have been shared with your tenant that you want to query using GraphQL requests.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the application name.
  4. Click the Tenant Access tab.
    Note: The number of tenants with access displays on the tab name.
  5. Under Access Resources From Other Tenants, click Add Resource.
  6. Select a tenant from the list, select the resources that were shared with you that you would like to subscribe to, and click Add.
    Note: If a resource is owned by other applications, you can select which application you want to add it with.

Subscribe to a resource from another tenant

You can subscribe to the owned resources from another tenant.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration, and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  3. On the Applications page, locate and click the application name.
  4. Click the Subscriptions tab.
  5. Click Add Subscriptions > Add Resources by Tenant.
  6. Select the tenant and the owned resources you want to subscribe to and click Add.

Configure Tenant Access

As a grantor, you can share resources that are owned by applications in your tenant and configure the credentials that will be used by that tenant for API requests.

As a grantee, you can select resources that have been shared with your tenant that you want to query using GraphQL requests. You can subscribe to the owned resources from another tenant.

Grant access to resource configurations your tenant owns

You can prevent an application from accessing certain properties within an added resource by hiding the properties.

About this task

For example, you might have loaded persons data into Data Access from Banner or Colleague. You want this application to be able to access most persons information, but not the dateOfBirth property. You would add the persons resource and then use the steps below to hide the dateOfBirth property.

Note: For examples of attribute filter setup, see Example attribute filters for GraphQL resources.

Procedure

  1. In the table of resources, locate the resource that contains the property you want to hide, and click Show more at the end of the row.
  2. In the Attribute Filters area, click Add .
  3. In the Path field, enter the path to the property that you want to hide.
    For example, to hide the date of birth property in the persons resource, you enter /dateOfBirth.

    To determine the path to a property, go to the API Catalog, navigate to the API documentation page for the version and product that you are interested in viewing, scroll down to the schemas section and expand to view properties.

  4. If you want the property to be hidden from this application only under certain conditions, click Add Criteria and then enter the criteria:
    Field Entry
    Property Path Enter the path to the data model property to be used in the criterion. This property must be in the same resource as the property that you are hiding.
    Operator Select equals or not equals
    Criteria Enter the value of this property that will determine whether the criterion is met.
  5. After defining all filters for this resource, click Save.
    In this case, if you change the resource permissions and you invoke a GraphQL query immediately after, the resource will still have the old configuration for 30 minutes, unless you invoke GraphQL with the reset-cache header. This header when set to any value does reset the GraphQL cache, which makes the resource change effective immediately for that current GraphQL query invocation.

Provision OAuth credentials in the ERP

Perform these procedures to create OAuth credentials (an OAuth client ID and secret) in Banner or Colleague. These credentials are used in creating OAuth tokens that the ERP uses to securely access other Ellucian solutions.

This documentation contains one-time procedures for using Ethos Integration to create OAuth credentials in the ERP. For each integration that uses an OAuth token, the procedures for that integration include using the OAuth credentials to create an OAuth token.

The same set of credentials can be used to create the OAuth tokens for all integrations. You can check whether the credentials already exist using Step 6 in Create the OAuth credentials in the ERP. If the credentials already exist, you can skip these procedures.

Note: For Banner Multi-Entity Processing (MEP) implementations, perform these procedures for each MEP instance.

Set up the ERP to support OAuth credential provisioning

The provisioning of OAuth credentials requires setup of the ERP APIs and a user account in the ERP with permissions to write the credentials.

ERP API setup

The ERP API must own the Ethos resource that supports OAuth credential provisioning.

ERP Setup requirements
Banner The Banner Business Process API must be set up in Ethos Integration and must be the owner of the application-configurations resource.

This requires Banner General 9.3.30 or later, which is the Banner General version where the application-configurations resource was introduced.
Colleague The Colleague Web API must be set up in Ethos Integration and must be the owner of the oauth-configurations resource.

This requires Colleague Web API 2.2 or later, which is the Colleague Web API version where the oauth-configurations resource was introduced.

User account setup

Set up a user account in the ERP with permissions to write the credentials to the ERP.

ERP Setup requirements
Banner Either create a new Banner user account, or update an existing user account, with administrator access to the GUACONF page, which supports writing OAuth credentials to the GUROCFG table.
Colleague Either create a new Colleague user, or update an existing user, to have the UPDATE.CONFIG.SETTING permission, which supports provisioning of OAuth credentials.

Add the oauth-credentials resource to the Experience platform component

The Ethos platform component for Ellucian Experience must own the oauth-credentials resource to support the provisioning process.

About this task

Validating the Experience API key, which is part of basic Ellucian Experience setup, automatically adds the oauth-credentials resource to the Experience platform component. This capability was introduced with Experience 1.85. If you have validated the Experience API key after the release of Experience 1.85, you don't need to validate it again, although you should confirm that the resource was successfully added as described in Step 4 below.

Procedure

  1. Access Ellucian Experience Setup:
    1. In the Ellucian Customer Center, click Tools and then select the desired Experience Setup instance under the Experience category:
      • Click Experience Setup to access the Production instance of Experience Setup.
      • Click Experience Setup Test to access the Test instance of Experience Setup.
    2. (If applicable) In Experience Setup, in the Environments menu, select the desired Ethos environment.
      The option to select an environment is available only if multiple Ethos environments are associated with this Experience Setup instance.
  2. Click the Dashboard Setup tab.
  3. In the Dashboard Access section of the page, click Validate.
    Validation automatically adds the oauth-credentials resource to the Experience platform component.
  4. In Ethos Integration, confirm that the resource was successfully added:
    1. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click the gear button and then select the same Ethos environment you selected in Experience Setup.
    2. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Platform Components.
    3. On the Ethos Platform Components page, locate the Ellucian Experience tile and click View.
    4. On the Ethos Platform Component Overview page, click the Owned Resources tab.
    5. Confirm that oauth-credentials is in the list of owned resources.

Set up an Ethos application for OAuth credential provisioning

Configure the Ethos application that supports the provisioning process.

About this task

Provisioning of OAuth credentials in the ERP requires an Ethos application that includes the credentials of the user account described in Set up the ERP to support OAuth credential provisioning. There are several possibilities:
  • You can create a new Ethos application and add the user credentials, as described in the procedure below.
  • You can use an existing Ethos application and add the user credentials to that application, as described in the procedure below.
  • If you added the required ERP permissions to an existing user account (rather than creating a new user account), and if you already have an existing Ethos application with that user's credentials, you can skip this procedure.

Procedure

  1. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  2. If you are adding the user credentials to an existing Ethos application, click the name of that application in the Application Name column. Then skip to Step 4 to add the credentials.
    Otherwise, continue with Step 3 to create a new Ethos application.
  3. Create the Ethos application:
    1. In the Create New App area of the page, click Manually.
    2. In the Add Application dialog box, accept the defaults and click Continue.
    3. On the Add Application page, enter a name for the application and then click Next.
      Example name: Provision OAuth credentials
    4. On the Add Subscriptions page, click Skip.
    5. Click View Application to go to the Application Overview page where you will configure the application.
  4. On the Application Overview page, click the Credentials tab.
  5. On the Credentials tab, click Add Credentials.
  6. In the Add Credentials dialog box, enter the settings below.
    Field Banner entry Colleague entry
    Source application Select the Ethos application for the Banner Business Process API (the Ethos application that owns the application-configurations resource). Select the Ethos application for the Colleague Web API (the Ethos application that owns the oauth-configurations resource).
    Username Enter the credentials for the Banner user account that you set up in Set up the ERP to support OAuth credential provisioning. Enter the credentials for the Colleague user account that you set up in Set up the ERP to support OAuth credential provisioning.
    Password
    Select a resource Select application-configurations Select oauth-configurations
  7. Click Add Credentials.

Set up the Experience platform component for OAuth credential provisioning

The Ethos platform component for Experience must have access to the ERP API (Banner Business Process API or Colleague Web API).

Procedure

  1. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Platform Components.
  2. On the Ethos Platform Components page, locate the Ellucian Experience tile and click View.
  3. On the Ethos Platform Component Overview page, click the Application Access tab.
  4. On the Application Access tab, click Add Application Access.
  5. In the Add Application Access dialog box, select the Ethos application that you created for OAuth credential provisioning (or the existing application that you are using) as described in Set up an Ethos application for OAuth credential provisioning.
  6. Click Add.

Create the OAuth credentials in the ERP

Send the POST request through Ethos Integration that creates the OAuth credentials in Banner or Colleague.

About this task

You can use a REST API client to generate an Ethos token and send the POST request. The steps below use cURL examples to show the required code.

Procedure

  1. Perform the steps below to copy the API key for the Ethos application that you created for OAuth credential provisioning.
    You will use this key when generating an Ethos token in Step 2.
    1. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
    2. On the Applications page, select the application that you configured using the procedure in Set up an Ethos application for OAuth credential provisioning.
    3. On the Application Overview page, click the API Keys tab (the default).
    4. On the API Keys page, locate the row for the API key and click Copy .
  2. Generate an Ethos token by making a request to the Ethos Integration authorization service.

    You can use a REST API client to generate the Ethos token. This cURL example shows the code that would get the Ethos token.

    curl -X POST 
-H "Authorization: Bearer {api_key}" 
-H "Cache-Control: no-cache" 'https://integrate.elluciancloud.com/auth'
    • For {api_key}, substitute the API key that you copied in Step 1.d.
    • If you are in a region other than the U.S., substitute the domain for your region in place of integrate.elluciancloud.com. See Ethos Integration domains.
  3. From the response to that request, copy the generated Ethos token.
  4. Send the POST request that provisions the credentials in the ERP.

    You can use a REST API client to send the POST request. This cURL example shows the code that would provision the credentials.

    curl -i -X POST \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {ethos_token}' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
    "tenant":{
        "id": "{tenant_id}"
    },
    "app": "{erp_name}"
}' \
https://integrate.elluciancloud.com/api/oauth-credentials
    • For {ethos_token}, substitute the token that you copied in Step 3.
    • For {tenant_id}, substitute the ID for your Ethos tenant. You can copy that ID from the top right of any page in Ethos Integration.
    • For {erp_name}, enter banner or colleague.
    • If you are in a region other than the U.S., substitute the domain for your region in place of integrate.elluciancloud.com. See Ethos Integration domains.

    Colleague example:

    curl -i -X POST \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUz​I1NiIsInR5cCI6I​kpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ​lYzcwODc1OC01Nm​U1LTQ2NGYtYmI5Yi0​3ZmI4Y2M4M2E1N​DMiLCJ0b2ciOls​iZmVhdHVyZV9i​ZXRhIl0sInRlbmF​udCI6eyJpZCI6I​mRhZGE0ZDM0LWQzY​zAtZGFkZS1kNmV​kLWQ5ZmMyMDEzMT​U5ZiIsImFjY29​1bnRJZCI6IkV​sb3ljZSBVbml2Z​XJzaXR5IiwiYWxpYXMi​OiJlbG95Y2V0ZXN0I​iwibmFtZSI6IkV​sb3ljZSBUZ​XN0IiwibGFiZWwiO​iJUZXN0In0sImFwaUtle​VByZWZpeCI6IjkyZDc3Kio​qKioqKioqKioqKioqKio​qKioqKioqKioqKioqKiI​sImlhdCI6MTc0MjM​xOTE3OCwiZXhwI​joxNzQyMzE5NDc4​fQ.hwBjZMNEsEvlamVS6N​vk87Lb9AOUeiI1​FV4OKzhK9-k' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
    "tenant":{
        "id": "4fe349d5-0d68-4df6-bd29-a3a112054e7f"
    },
    "app": "colleague"
}' \
https://integrate.elluciancloud.com/api/oauth-credentials

  5. Check the response to the POST request, and then proceed based on the code returned in the response. Use the appropriate table below for your ERP.
    Table 1. Banner
    Code What this indicates Next step
    201 The POST request successfully provisioned the credentials in Banner, or no update was needed because the credentials already exist in Banner from a previous POST request. Go to Step 6 to confirm that the credentials exist in Banner.
    424 This might indicate a problem with the provisioning process, or it might indicate that no update was made because credentials already exist in Banner and there is a problem with those credentials. Go to Step 6 to check whether the credentials exist in Banner.
    • If credentials don't exist, there was a problem that prevented the process from running successfully. Review these procedures to check your Ethos setup and then try the POST request again.
    • If credentials exist, delete them and then send the POST request again to provision new credentials. To delete the existing credentials, access the GLOBAL application on the GUACONF page as described in Step 6, and delete all four configurations listed in Step 6.d.
    Table 2. Colleague
    Code What this indicates Next step
    201 The POST request successfully provisioned the credentials in Colleague. Go to Step 6 to confirm that the credentials exist in Colleague.
    424 This might indicate a problem with the provisioning process, or it might indicate that no update was made because credentials already exist in Colleague and there is a problem with those credentials. Go to Step 6 to check whether the credentials exist in Colleague.
    • If credentials don't exist, there was a problem that prevented the process from running successfully. Review these procedures to check your Ethos setup and then try the POST request again.
    • If credentials exist, delete them and then send the POST request again to provision new credentials. To delete the existing credentials, access the COLLEAGUE configuration on the OACF form as described in Step 6, and do a record delete to delete the COLLEAGUE configuration.
  6. Check the ERP to confirm that the credentials were successfully provisioned.
    For Banner:
    1. Access the GUACONF page.
    2. In the Application ID field, enter GLOBAL.
    3. Click the Configurations tab and then filter Configuration Name for %banner.oauth% to find all configurations containing banner.oauth.
    4. Review the entries on the page.
      The following configurations should be displayed:
      • banner.oauth.clientid - This value should match the clientId in the response to the POST request.
      • banner.oauth.clientSecret
      • banner.oauth.oauthEndpoint
      • banner.oauth.resource

    For Colleague:

    1. Access the OAuth Configuration (OACF) form.
    2. At the OAuth Configuration Lookup prompt, access the COLLEAGUE configuration.
    3. Review the entries on the form.

      The Client ID field should contain a value that matches the clientId in the response to the POST request.
